fields.精确定义: A type of machine system designed by humans that can generate outputs such as predictions, recommendations, or decisions based on given goals, and its operation demonstrates the ability to perform tasks that usually require human intelligence.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "AI thinks, is conscious, and has emotions like humans"; or AI is equated with robots (AI is software capability, robots are hardware carriers, and the two can exist independently).
fields.典型案例: The mobile phone voice assistant converts the words into text and answers; the map software calculates the recommended route.
fields.反例: Call a calculator that can do arithmetic as AI; call an automatic door with only a fixed circuit as AI.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the intuitive impression of "what it can do and how it can be done" and does not talk about the internal structure of the system.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The output of AI is determined by the goals and data designed by humans and does not bear human responsibility.
fields.教学类比: It can be compared to a "machine assistant that can do work", but it must be pointed out: it has no understanding, no intention, and no responsibility.
fields.来源依据: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (AI is defined as a machine-based system that can generate predictions, recommendations, or decisions under given goals)
fields.通俗解释:
To put it bluntly, artificial intelligence is a type of machine system: people set a goal for it, and it can make predictions, suggestions or decisions on its own, and it does things that usually require people to use their brains. Mobile phone voice assistants can turn what you say into text and reply back, and map software can calculate the fastest way to go. These are all helping people do things that "should be thought about".
Seize two key points: first, it is man-made, and its goals are set by people - no matter how capable it is, it still revolves around the goals given by people; second, it only produces results and does not take responsibility. It's like hiring a good helper. The idea comes up, but the responsibility is still yours.
There is one thing that is easy to confuse: AI is the ability in the software, and the robot is the hardware shell, and the two sides can exist separately: the voice assistant has no body, but it is also AI; the robotic arm that can only fix its movements can still move without AI. The calculator does not count as AI, as it follows rigid rules; the automatic door does not count, as it is just set to "open when someone comes".
You can think of AI as a "machine assistant that can do work", but it has no understanding, no ideas, and no responsibility. Keeping these three in mind will make it easy to understand a whole bunch of concepts that follow.

fields.精确定义: The ability of an individual or system to achieve goals in a specific environment, such as identifying patterns, reasoning, planning, and adapting to new situations.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "intelligence is only possessed by humans"; or the misunderstanding is that "being able to do something means that there is intelligence" (ability does not mean having consciousness).
fields.典型案例: People recognize familiar faces; chess-playing programs make good moves.
fields.反例: Think of "being able to repeat an action" as intelligence, such as an escalator.
fields.深度上限: Only "performance of what can be accomplished" is discussed, and inconclusive issues such as consciousness and emotion are not discussed.
fields.安全与伦理边界: When discussing intelligence, avoid equating machine performance with the human mind.
fields.来源依据: Common subject definitions (Introduction to Cognitive Science and AI Consensus)
fields.通俗解释:
To put it bluntly, intelligence is the ability to "get things done": the ability of an individual or system to achieve goals in a specific environment, such as recognizing patterns, reasoning, making plans, and coping with new situations. When people recognize familiar faces, this is intelligence; when a chess-playing program makes a good move, this is also intelligence. It is not a patent of humans. Whichever system can turn goals into results in the environment will have intelligence.
The basis for judgment is "ability performance." Being able to repeat a certain action does not count: an escalator sends people to one level every day, and its movements are fixed and cannot be adjusted according to the environment, so it cannot be said to be intelligent. It's like two drivers. One can read the road conditions and avoid traffic jams, while the other can only idle along the drawn line. The difference lies in whether he can adapt to the situation and drive the car to the destination.
There is also a rule of thumb: Just because a machine behaves intelligently does not mean it is conscious. This lesson only talks about "what can be accomplished" and "what does it think in its heart" and other inconclusive questions will be left aside for now. Just because it behaves like a human being does not mean that there is a human being living inside.

fields.精确定义: Human beings form abilities through learning and experience, and have consciousness, emotion and sociality; machines form abilities through calculation and statistics of data, and their output is determined by parameters and algorithms.
fields.常见误解: The capabilities displayed by machines are directly equated to the same capabilities of humans; "output like humans" is regarded as "having human attributes".
fields.典型案例: Machines can quickly translate full text, but they don’t understand the feelings brought about by the text.
fields.反例: Replace "AI comforts people" with "AI cares about you."
fields.深度上限: We only talk about observable differences and differences in operating methods, and do not discuss inconclusive issues such as "Can machines be conscious?"
fields.安全与伦理边界: The difference is the basis for "human responsibility cannot be transferred".
fields.教学类比: The “partner” analogy can help understand collaborative relationships, but AI does not have human understanding, intention, and responsibility.
fields.来源依据: Master §3.1 K1 Boundary + Introduction to General AI
fields.通俗解释:
Both humans and machines can accomplish things, but in completely different ways. Human abilities develop little by little through learning and experience, and are accompanied by consciousness, emotion, and sociality; machine abilities come from the calculation and statistics of data, and each of its outputs is determined by parameters and algorithms.
The difference is observable: a machine can translate an entire article in the blink of an eye, but it cannot experience the feeling behind the words. Therefore, the accurate expression of the statement "AI will comfort people" is "AI will output words to comfort people" - outputting like a human does not mean it has human attributes. It is the most common confusion method to directly regard the performance of a machine as the same ability as a human.
When dealing with AI, the term "partner" can help understand the collaborative relationship, but remember: partners have understanding, intention, and responsibility, but AI does not have these three things. These differences are the basis for "human responsibility cannot be transferred".

fields.精确定义: Describes the basic model of information system operation: receiving input data, processing it through algorithms, and producing output results.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the output is the result that the system "wants"" (the output is determined by the input and the algorithm).
fields.典型案例: Translation software: input Chinese sentences → process → output English sentences.
fields.反例: The reason for "the output is not as required" is attributed to "the AI doesn't want to do it".
fields.深度上限: It only makes observations of "looking for input and output" and does not deal with internal details.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Input may contain personal information and output may contain errors, both of which require human review.
fields.通俗解释:
There is a basic process for working in an information system: data is received, processed by algorithms, and finally the results are given. These three steps are called input, processing, and output. Translation software is a ready-made example. It inputs a Chinese sentence, processes it, and outputs an English sentence.
When observing any AI system, you can do two things first: look for input and look for output. How to calculate it in the middle, don’t worry about it for now. The important thing is to understand: the output is determined by the input and the algorithm, not the result the system itself "wants". When the output does not meet the requirements, don't attribute it to "the AI ​​doesn't want to do it." It doesn't think about it. It's this set of inputs and this set of algorithms that calculates the result.
This process is like a processing assembly line: the assembly line does not choose what materials to put in, what processes to go through, and what finished products to produce. There are two other places where people have to check: the input may contain personal information, and the output may contain errors.

fields.精确定义: AI systems that only have capabilities in specific tasks or limited areas, such as face recognition, speech transcription, and chess games. Also called “Specialized Artificial Intelligence” – it doesn’t work in another field.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "narrow AI can do everything"; or the excellent performance of narrow AI is regarded as evidence of general intelligence; or "narrow/specialized" means "poor technology" (it is only limited in scope, and often far surpasses humans in that matter).
fields.典型案例: A translation model that only does translation; a game program that only plays Go.
fields.反例: He believes that "a program that can play chess can also write essays."
fields.深度上限: Just know that "most of the existing AIs are specialists" and do not use taxonomic terms.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Do not exaggerate your overall ability just because you perform well on a certain task.
fields.教学类比: Like a plumber who only knows how to fix pipes - he's good at fixing pipes, but don't let him do your dental work.
fields.来源依据: Common AI classification (Narrow / General / Super AI); the translation of "Special Artificial Intelligence" can be found in People's Daily 2023-06-26
fields.通俗解释:
Narrow artificial intelligence refers to AI that is only capable of specific tasks and limited areas, such as face recognition, speech transcription, and chess games. It is also called special artificial intelligence, and it has one characteristic: it will not work in another field. If you only make a translation model and let it play chess, it will not be able to play; if you only make a Go program and let it write an article, you will not be able to write it.
Don’t mistake “narrow” for “poor technology.” It's just that its scope is very limited, and it often far surpasses humans in the one thing it's limited to. It will not “know a little bit of everything” and its abilities will not be overflowed. When you see a certain AI performing well, you take it as evidence of general intelligence, which is also overthinking.
For example, it is like a plumber who only knows how to repair water pipes: he is a good man at repairing water pipes, but don’t let him check your teeth. To judge whether an AI is narrow or wide, it depends on how much ability it has left behind its original line of work.

fields.精确定义: Refers to artificial intelligence that reaches or exceeds human levels on a wide range of tasks, rather than excelling at just a single task. It is a goal and concept that is debated in the industry. It has not yet been realized and there is no generally accepted criterion.
fields.常见误解: Think of today's powerful chatbots as AGI; or think of AGI as a technology node that "the time is determined and will definitely come".
fields.典型案例: Discuss "AI can write code and draw, is it close to AGI?" and analyze the difference between "versatile" and "general intelligence".
fields.反例: Consider “being able to pass a certain test” as evidence of AGI.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "goals, controversies, and why it is difficult to determine" and does not talk about implementation paths and technical routes.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Avoid packaging the AGI narrative into inevitable conclusions or marketing rhetoric.
fields.教学类比: Like a "universal player who can do everything", but today all AIs are still "specialized players".
fields.来源依据: Common industry definition; Master §3.1 K1 “General Artificial Intelligence”
fields.通俗解释:
General artificial intelligence refers to AI that "can do anything to the human level" - it is not just good at one thing, but it can reach or even surpass humans in a wide range of tasks. It can draw inferences from one case to another: today I learned to play chess, and tomorrow I will use this set of skills to learn to write code and learn to treat patients. The existing knowledge can be used for new tasks.
Here we need to distinguish between assumptions and reality: AGI is still a target of debate in the industry. It has not been implemented, and there is no generally accepted standard for "how to judge if it has been achieved." No matter how well the current AI can talk or write, it is still working within the scope of its own design and training, and it is still far from being "capable of everything".
For example, today's AI is like a group of specialists who specialize in one area, while AGI is an all-rounder who can handle everything. The whole world is still wondering how to create the first one, and they are still arguing about "to what extent does it count?"
Be careful: some people claim that "AGI already exists", let me ask first - what standard is used to calculate it? Those who can't answer it are probably just propaganda talk.

fields.精确定义: Refers to a hypothetical intelligence that far exceeds that of the smartest humans in almost every aspect. It is a visionary concept for the future, used primarily to discuss risk and governance rather than existing technologies.
fields.常见误解: Confusing ASI with AGI; mistaking images of ASI in science fiction as predictions of reality.
fields.典型案例: Discussing "How can humans maintain dominance if intelligence far beyond humans emerges" raises the issue of controllability.
fields.反例: Think of the movie plot as a technical roadmap.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about “scenarios, risk issues, and why they are worth thinking about in advance” and does not predict the time or form.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Distinguish between "future assumptions" and "current facts" during discussions, and do not create panic or make commitments about capabilities.
fields.来源依据: Bostrom's "Superintelligence" and other popular discussions; master version §3.1 K1
fields.通俗解释:
The so-called superintelligence refers to a hypothetical intelligence that far exceeds the smartest human beings in almost all aspects. Pay attention to the word "hypothesis": it is a hypothetical concept for the future. It does not exist at the moment, and no one can tell when it will appear and what form it will take. People mention it mainly to discuss risks and governance: If intelligence far beyond humans really emerges, how can humans maintain dominance? This is how the issue of controllability arises.
There are two confusions to avoid: first, don’t equate it with AGI. AGI means “everything can live at the human level”, while superintelligence means “surpassing the smartest human beings in almost all aspects”. The levels are different; second, don’t use the images of robots in science fiction movies as realistic predictions. Movies are stories, not technology roadmaps.
For example, this is like urban planners discussing "what if there is a once-in-a-hundred-year flood." The flood does not come, but drainage and evacuation must be thought out in advance. Discussing a hypothetical danger is not the same as believing that it will happen tomorrow.

fields.精确定义: A judgment idea proposed by Alan Turing in 1950: If the tester cannot distinguish whether the conversation partner is a human or a machine through text communication, the machine is considered to have passed the test.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "passing the Turing test means that the machine has consciousness or real thinking" (the test only measures external conversational performance, not internal state).
fields.典型案例: In 1950, Turing proposed the idea of "imitation games" in "Computing Machines and Intelligence".
fields.反例: Take "cheating" as proof of "consciousness."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "the external performance is measured, not the inner heart" and does not talk about the technical implementation and debate history of the test.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Do not take the test results as evidence that the machine has personality.
fields.来源依据: A. M. Turing, “Computing Machinery and Intelligence”, Mind, 1950
fields.通俗解释:
In 1950, Turing proposed a way to answer the question "Can machines think?": Don't argue about definitions, test it directly. It allows you to chat with two parties using text across the screen, one is a human and the other is a machine. If you can't tell who is the machine, then the machine will pass. This is the Turing test.
The clever thing about it is that it replaces the noisy question of "thinking" with the actionable question of "can it be recognized?" But it is just an ideological judgment, not a strict examination: passing it does not mean that the machine is really intelligent; failing it does not mean that the machine is useless. What it reflects is "the degree of imitation of people", not "the degree of intelligence".
It's like tasting tea while blindfolded and guessing the place of origin - guessing correctly means that it is pretending to be similar, but it does not mean that the tea mountain has the same flavor.
Remember its positioning: a first-of-its-kind judgment idea. It is two different things from "machine can really think".

fields.精确定义: A framework describing the operation cycle of an intelligent system: first obtain environmental information (perception), then calculate and select actions based on it (decision-making), and finally execute actions to affect the environment (action).
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "it must have all three links to be called AI" (many systems only cover some of these links).
fields.典型案例: Sweeping robot: Perceive obstacles → Decide to turn → Execute movement.
fields.反例: A timer that only "executes" is said to have aware decision-making.
fields.深度上限: Only link identification and sorting are done, and control theory and algorithm implementation are not discussed.
fields.安全与伦理边界: "Decisions" are made by humans who set goals and limits, and humans retain the right to stop.
fields.来源依据: Common framework for control and robotics
fields.通俗解释:
When an intelligent system is running, it is common to go through a cycle: first obtain environmental information, which is called perception; then calculate and select an action based on it, which is called decision-making; and finally execute the action and affect the environment, which is called action. You can see clearly after walking around the sweeping robot: encountering obstacles is perception, deciding where to turn is decision-making, and actually turning around is action.
The whole cycle is like a person reaching out for a glass of water: the eyes see where the glass is, the brain decides how to reach out, and then the hand moves. This framework is easy to use, but there is a misunderstanding that needs to be eliminated: only the three links must be put together to be called AI. Many systems only cover part of it. On the other hand, you cannot say that it has perception and decision-making just because you see "can execute" - it will start when the timer expires, and it will only execute, and the first two links are empty.
The correct way to use it is to sequence the behavior of the system step by step: which step is sensing, which step is decision-making, and which step is action. Another thing to remember: the goals and limits of the decision-making process are set by people, and the stop switch is also in people's hands.

fields.精确定义: AI systems are effective within the range of their training data, design goals, and operating conditions. Output reliability decreases beyond this range.
fields.常见误解: Misunderstanding that "AI is omnipotent and always correct"; or attributing errors to "it has emotions and subjective will".
fields.典型案例: On questions where the training corpus is rare, the model is more likely to give wrong answers.
fields.反例: Treat the AI's confident tone as reliable evidence.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "there are boundaries and errors will occur" and does not introduce probability and loss functions.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Capability boundaries are the direct reason for "manual verification is required".
fields.通俗解释:
Every AI system has a capability boundary: it is valid within the scope of its own training data, design goals, and operating conditions. Once exceeded, the reliability of the output will drop. Ask it questions that are rarely seen in the training materials, and the possibility of making mistakes will obviously increase. This is a normal behavior after exceeding the range.
Both extreme impressions must be let go. One is that "AI is omnipotent and always correct", which is not true. It has a clear scope of application; the other is that "it is emotional and has subjective will" when it makes mistakes, which is also not true. It just gives unreliable results outside the scope. There is another pitfall: the more confident the AI ​​speaks, the more people will take it seriously, but the tone is the expression style, not reliable evidence.
Just like a familiar chef may fail if he loses his specialty cuisine, the same may happen if AI leaves its original profession. Precisely because the boundary is there, manual verification is not a polite word, but a necessary step when using AI.

fields.精确定义: The degree to which a system can complete a series of operations on its own according to established goals without manual intervention; autonomy can be divided into different levels.
fields.常见误解: Misunderstood as "autonomy = having free will or independent consciousness" (autonomy refers to the degree of intervention in operation and is an engineering attribute).
fields.典型案例: The automated parking system completes a full set of actions; the chatbot only responds to a single wheel of input.
fields.反例: Say "automatically play the next episode" as "AI autonomous decision".
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the engineering meaning of "how much people are involved" and does not talk about consciousness and personality.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The higher the autonomy, the more necessary it is to set up manual judgment points and stopping conditions.
fields.来源依据: NIST AI RMF：“AI systems are designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy”
fields.通俗解释:
The word autonomy sounds mysterious, but the engineering meaning is very simple: the system completes a series of operations according to the set goals without manual intervention step by step. The degree of "human intervention" is the degree of autonomy. It is divided into levels - the automatic parking system can complete the entire set of positioning actions in one go, with little human intervention; the chatbot only responds to a single round of input, saying and answering, with more human intervention.
It has nothing to do with "free will" or "independent consciousness". Autonomy describes the degree of human intervention in operation and is a purely engineering attribute. According to this standard, "automatically playing the next episode" is not considered an autonomous decision by the AI. It is because the rules written in advance were triggered, not by it making a decision.
Think of it like flying a kite: the longer the string, the farther the kite flies, but the spool is always in the person's hand. The higher the autonomy, the more it is necessary to set up manual judgment points and stopping conditions. This is a corresponding requirement in engineering.

fields.精确定义: The calculator performs fixed, closed arithmetic functions, and the input-output relationship is predetermined by the hardware circuit; the computer is a general-purpose machine that can execute replaceable programs and can handle a variety of tasks.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "a machine that can count is a computer"; or "calculators also have intelligence" (calculators do not have programmable versatility and learning capabilities).
fields.典型案例: The same computer can play videos and write documents; a calculator can only do arithmetic.
fields.反例: Consider "simple but fast" as evidence of intelligence.
fields.深度上限: Just do the comparison of "fixed functions vs replaceable programs".
fields.来源依据: General content of computer composition principles
fields.通俗解释:
They are both machines that can count, and there is only one difference: whether they can change the program. The calculator only does fixed arithmetic tasks, such as how to calculate addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, and what is the relationship between input and output. It is welded into the circuit when it leaves the factory. Whatever you press will produce something, and it will never be able to create new tricks. A computer is different. It is a general-purpose machine. It can do any job with whatever program it is installed on - processing forms today, editing videos tomorrow, and training AI models the day after tomorrow.
This boundary is used to understand "what is intelligence": being able to count does not equal intelligence. No matter how fast the calculator calculates, it still follows strict rules; the machine can change programs and do different jobs, and only then can we talk about the word "intelligence".
To use an analogy: a calculator is like a vending machine that only sells one kind of drink. It is coin-operated and remains unchanged for decades; a computer is like a fully functional kitchen, and you can cook whatever you want by changing the recipe.
Next time you hear someone say "this machine is so smart," ask first: does it only know one set of fixed actions, or can it do different tasks in different ways?

fields.精确定义: There are various relationships between people and technical systems, such as the use of tools, joint decision-making, and autonomous operation of the system. People have different roles and responsibilities under different relationships.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "humans and AI can only have a substitute relationship" (there are also relationships such as enhancement, collaboration, supervision, etc.).
fields.典型案例: In navigation-assisted driving, people still have to keep an eye on the road and take over at any time.
fields.反例: Treat "AI makes suggestions" as "AI has decided".
fields.深度上限: Only the types of relationships that students can be exposed to are discussed, and organizational management theory is not discussed.
fields.安全与伦理边界: In any relationship, important decisions involving rights and security must be made by people.
fields.来源依据: Master version §3.1 K1 + §2.3 Concept of human-machine collaboration
fields.通俗解释:
There is more than one way for people to get along with technical systems: sometimes people use it as a tool, sometimes both parties participate in decisions together, and sometimes the system runs by itself while people watch from the side. Different relationships have different roles and responsibilities.
The most misunderstanding that should be eliminated is that "when AI comes, it will replace people." Substitution is just one of them. In addition, there is enhancement, which helps people amplify their abilities; there is collaboration, where everyone does what they are good at; there is supervision, where the system runs and people watch. Assisted driving is a ready-made example: the system can lead the way, but the driver still has to keep an eye on the road and be ready to take over at any time. The responsibility does not leave the person because of the addition of an additional system.
It's like the same pen: it's a tool when helping people keep accounts, it's a partner when discussing with others to draft a plan, and it's the party being supervised when it's finished and waiting for others to review and revise it - when the roles change, the responsibilities change accordingly. So when you see "AI has made suggestions", don't slip into "AI has made a decision"; important decisions involving rights and security must be made by humans in any relationship.

1-14.name: Division of Labour and Responsibility in Human–AI Collaboration

fields.精确定义: Allocate work between humans, AI, and common tools based on task characteristics. Humans are responsible for goals, verifications, important decisions, and consequences, while AI does not bear responsibility.
fields.常见误解: Think of "AI has decided it for me" as "the decision can be made by AI".
fields.典型案例: Writing event notice: People set the goals and scope, AI drafts, people check the facts and wording and decide whether to publish it.
fields.反例: Publish the list generated by AI directly without checking whether other people's information is leaked.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "who does what and who is responsible" and does not talk about collaborative management theory.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Responsibility cannot be transferred to AI; decisions involving interests must be made by humans.
fields.教学类比: The “co-pilot” analogy is available, but the steering wheel and responsibility are always in the hands of the person.
fields.来源依据: Master version §1.5 Principles of human-machine collaboration + §2.3 Concept of human-machine collaboration
fields.通俗解释:
The division of labor in human-machine collaboration has a basic structure: according to the characteristics of the task, the work is divided into humans, AI and ordinary tools. Goals, verifications, important decisions, and consequences belong to humans; AI does not bear responsibility.
Go through the process of writing an event notice: humans set the goals and scope first, AI drafts the first draft, the facts and wording are checked by humans, and ultimately humans decide whether and how to publish it. There are also negative lessons: Some people directly send out the list generated by AI without checking it, and as a result, other people's information is leaked - the responsibility still lies with the person, AI will not take it for you.
Pay attention to the sentence "AI has thought it out for me": Having thought it through does not mean that the decision can be made by AI. The analogy of the co-pilot applies here: AI can help see the road and make suggestions, but the steering wheel and responsibility are in the hands of the human from beginning to end.

fields.精确定义: It means that the AI system participates in improving itself (changing code, changing training data, changing prompt strategies, etc.), and the improved version can continue to improve the next generation, forming a cycle of "accelerating itself". At present, prototypes have appeared in engineering (AI generates training data, self-criticism, self-playing, and intelligent agents independently optimize their own configuration), but an uncontrolled and out-of-control closed loop has not yet been formed.
fields.常见误解: They think that RSI is just a purely theoretical idea that has not yet been implemented; or conversely, they think that "AI is already evolving on its own and is about to get out of control."
fields.典型案例: Understand the ongoing engineering practice of "using AI-generated data to train stronger AI" and think about the difference between it and "out of control".
fields.反例: Exaggerating "automatic parameter adjustment of the model" to "AI has independent will".
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "what it is, to what extent it is now, and why it is a security issue" without developing technical implementation.
fields.安全与伦理边界: RSI changes "controllability" from a long-term concern to a current issue, and the discussion must be based on engineering facts rather than science fiction imagination.
fields.教学类比: For example, "Students will set their own questions for themselves to complete, and they can change more difficult questions after completing them." However, the standards and purposes of setting questions are still set by people.
fields.来源依据: 2024-2026 AI self-improvement/self-reward/synthetic data reinfusion and other engineering practices; Master Version §3.1 K1
fields.通俗解释:
Recursive self-improvement means that the AI participates in improving the AI itself: let the AI change the code, change the training data, and change the prompt strategy. The new version can then improve the next generation - going round and round, speeding up the AI itself. This is not pure science fiction. There are already prototypes in the project: using the data generated by AI to train stronger AI, allowing the model to self-criticize and find its own faults, and the AI ​​to autonomously optimize its own configuration, are all considered a small part of this cycle. But you have to be careful: an uncontrolled, out-of-control closed loop has not yet formed, and the loop is still spinning within human settings and constraints.
Why is it important? Because once "AI improves AI" starts to change, the speed of progress may exceed people's expectations, and "controllability" changes from a long-term concern to an immediate issue, so security discussions cannot avoid it. For example, students can set their own questions for themselves to complete, and can change more difficult questions after completing them. They are very capable - but the standards and purposes of setting questions are still set by the teacher.
There are two extremes to avoid: one is "pure theory", the other is "imminently out of control". The engineering facts are in the middle.

fields.精确定义: AI did not appear overnight: the term "artificial intelligence" was proposed at the Dartmouth Conference in 1956, and then experienced two "cold winters" (expectations were dashed and funds were withdrawn). In 2012, AlexNet set off a wave of deep learning, in 2017 Transformer laid the foundation for large models, and in 2022 ChatGPT brought AI to the masses. If you understand this line, you will understand that today's AI is the result of long-term accumulation and several breakthroughs.
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "AI suddenly appeared in recent years"; ignoring the many "hot-cold" cycles in history.
fields.典型案例: Use a timeline to connect key nodes and discuss "why AI will experience a cold winter and why it can rise again."
fields.反例: Consider "There was no AI before ChatGPT" as fact.
fields.深度上限: It only establishes a sense of context of "history and ups and downs" and does not talk about the details of each incident and the gossip of the characters.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Hype and Winter Tips in History: Be enthusiastic but also rational about new technologies. Whenever there is a craze, the term "artificial intelligence" is often used to package common technologies that are not intelligent (researchers call it the "artificial intelligence effect"). The more craze there is, the more important it is to distinguish between propaganda and facts.
fields.教学类比: It's like watching a TV series rather than a snapshot - today's plot is accumulated in the past.
fields.来源依据: A general overview of the history of AI development
fields.通俗解释:
AI didn't appear overnight. In 1956, the term "artificial intelligence" was proposed at the Dartmouth Conference. Later, it fell into the cold winter twice. Expectations were frustrated, funds were withdrawn, and the field suddenly cooled down. In 2012, AlexNet set off a wave of deep learning; in 2017, Transformer laid the foundation for large models; in 2022, ChatGPT brought AI into the public eye.
Looking at this timeline, the most important thing to take away is the sense of context of "history and ups and downs": booms and winters come in turns, and today's AI is the result of long-term accumulation and several breakthroughs. The statement "There was no AI before ChatGPT" is not true.
It's like watching a TV series, instead of taking a snapshot, the current plot is accumulated episode by episode. There is another phenomenon worth remembering in history: during every boom, the term "artificial intelligence" is often used to package ordinary technologies that are not intelligent. Researchers call this the "artificial intelligence effect." For new technologies, you can have enthusiasm, but you cannot lack rationality.

fields.精确定义: It refers to the two recognized rulers used in the AI field to understand "what are the differences between different AIs", and the two types of AI measured using them.
fields.常见误解: They think that "AI is a big language model" and "there is only one technical route"; or they regard "being able to play chess" and "being able to chat" as the same technology; or they regard "surpassing humans in something" (such as AlphaGo, AlphaFold) as "having achieved general intelligence."
fields.典型案例: Put three examples together and compare "the differences in the way they learn": AlphaGo learned to play Go by playing against itself; AlphaFold learned to predict structures by relying on protein structure data; and the large language model learned to answer questions by reading massive texts. Another question: "Why can't AlphaGo change tasks, but the large language model can talk about everything?"
fields.反例: It is common sense to think that "AI only has one type of large model"; or to smooth out the fundamental differences between the two types of AI with "it is all AI"; or conversely, to think that "the large language model can talk about anything, so it is already a general artificial intelligence."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the names and usage of the two rulers, and the comparison of the differences between the two types of AI. It does not talk about the internal algorithm implementation of each school, nor the architectural details of each model.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Understanding the differences in routes helps to judge "what a certain type of AI is suitable for and what it is not suitable for" and avoid being misled by "AI is omnipotent"; it also helps to rationally view popular debates such as "whether large models are already general artificial intelligence".
fields.教学类比: The two rulers are like "looking at a person" from two angles: one is to ask "how did he develop this skill" (the master teaches you the formula/see the more you understand/learn from beatings), and the other is to ask "does he only do one thing or can he do everything?"
fields.来源依据: School: "Artificial Intelligence Discipline System: Connotation, Structure and Development Suggestions", Journal of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, "Three Major Research Schools of Artificial Intelligence" by People's Daily; Special/General: People's Daily 2023-06-26 "Emphasis on the Development of General Artificial Intelligence", Shanghai University of Finance and Economics Journal (Liu Kai et al., 2018); AlphaGo is a mixture of connectionism + behaviorism: People's Daily, Tsinghua University Zhang Yaqin "Technological Development and Future Prospects of Artificial Intelligence"
fields.通俗解释:
There is more than one approach within AI. To distinguish "what is the difference between different AIs", there are two recognized rulers. The first question is "How did you develop this skill?": AlphaGo learned to play Go by playing against itself, AlphaFold learned to predict structures by relying on protein structure data, and large language models learned to answer questions by reading massive texts. The second measure is "You can only do one thing, or you can do everything."
When the two rulers are measured, the difference is revealed: AlphaGo cannot change tasks, but the large language model can talk about anything. It just eliminates several misunderstandings: thinking that AI is just a big language model, thinking that "being able to play chess" and "being able to chat" are the same technology, or taking "surpassing humans in something" as "general intelligence has been realized", which cannot be measured.
Just like looking at a person, you can ask from two angles: Was the skill taught by a master, realized by oneself, or was it acquired through beatings? Is he only good at one thing, or is he good at everything? AI is divided into these two perspectives. Different routes lead to different things suitable for it.

fields.精确定义: Refers to the landmark event of AlphaGo defeating the top human Go player in 2016. It does not use "reading massive articles", but self-playing + reinforcement learning: playing millions of games with yourself, and figuring out better ways to play from winning and losing. It stands for "dedicated route" - just do the best at Go, and you won't be able to do another task. It predates ChatGPT by 6 years.
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "AlphaGo can do everything just like ChatGPT"; equating "surpassing humans in something" with "general intelligence".
fields.典型案例: Understand that AlphaGo learned Go by "playing millions of games with itself" and discuss "why it can't do anything else".
fields.反例: I thought “an AI that can play chess can also write essays.”
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the intuition of "learn to play chess through self-play and specialize in a single task", and does not talk about Monte Carlo tree search and network structure.
fields.安全与伦理边界: It is a typical example of "narrow AI" - no matter how powerful it is, it is only limited to one thing. Please don't exaggerate.
fields.教学类比: Like an athlete who has been training hard for ten years and only practices "shooting" - he can shoot more accurately than anyone else, but it won't work if he is asked to play football.
fields.来源依据: DeepMind AlphaGo (2016); notch named by users
fields.通俗解释:
In 2016, AlphaGo defeated the top human Go player, becoming an iconic scene in the history of AI. Its learning method is very special: instead of reading a large number of articles, it strengthens learning through self-playing chess. You play millions of chess games with yourself and figure out better ways to play from the wins and losses in each game. It appeared 6 years earlier than ChatGPT.
But its ability is nailed down to Go. It represents a "dedicated route", which means you can only achieve the ultimate in one thing, and it will not work in another task: being able to play chess does not mean being able to write essays; being able to surpass humans in something does not mean general intelligence. To think that AlphaGo and ChatGPT can do everything is to mix the two things together.
It is like an athlete who has worked hard for ten years and only practiced shooting. He can shoot more accurately than anyone else, but it doesn't work when he is dragged to play football. No matter how powerful it is, it can only do one thing. This is typical of narrow AI - don't exaggerate its overall ability just because of its unique skill.

fields.精确定义: Refers to using AI to help humans do scientific research. The most famous example is AlphaFold: it solves a problem that has plagued the biological community for 50 years - predicting the three-dimensional structure of proteins based on amino acid sequences with high speed and high accuracy. The structure of proteins determines how drugs are designed and how diseases are treated, so it is of great value in biomedicine, and researchers won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for this. This route represents "AI can not only chat, but also help scientists discover new knowledge."
fields.常见误解: Think of AlphaFold as "a chatting AI"; ignore that it belongs to the "dedicated + scientific data" route, rather than the general large model route.
fields.典型案例: Understanding "what proteins look like" has been an unsolved problem in biology for 50 years, and AlphaFold has basically solved it.
fields.反例: I thought "AI can only do things like chatting with people."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the value and positioning of "AI helps scientists solve problems and wins Nobel Prizes", but does not talk about protein folding principles and model architecture.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The attribution and open source sharing of AI scientific research results are issues worthy of discussion.
fields.教学类比: It's like giving a scientist a "super assistant who can calculate the answer instantly" - but the question must be asked by the scientist, and the judgment must be made by the scientist.
fields.来源依据: AlphaFold2 (2020 CASP14 Breakthrough); 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry; Notch named by users
fields.通俗解释:
AI can not only chat, but can also help scientists do research and discover new knowledge. This route is called AI doing science. The most famous example is AlphaFold. It solves a problem that has plagued the biological community for 50 years: predicting the three-dimensional structure of proteins based on amino acid sequences with high speed and high accuracy. The importance of this matter is that what the protein looks like directly determines how drugs are designed and how diseases are treated. For this reason, the researchers will win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2024.
Don’t think of it as “an AI that can chat”. It is a dedicated model with scientific data, and is not the same as a general-purpose large model.
It is like equipping scientists with a super assistant who can calculate the answer instantly: the calculation is very fast, but the question must be asked by the scientist, and it must be determined by the scientist how to judge the result and the next step. In addition, who owns the results of AI research and how to open source and share them are issues worthy of discussion.

fields.精确定义: Refers to the classification of AI according to "wide range of uses". Specialized artificial intelligence can only complete specific tasks through a specific set of algorithms, such as AlphaGo, which only plays Go, and AlphaFold, which only predicts protein structures; general artificial intelligence, which has the ability to transfer knowledge and can draw inferences and draw inferences like humans, and can use its knowledge to solve new tasks when encountering them, has not yet been realized.
fields.常见误解: Treat different translations as different concepts (see "narrow artificial intelligence" and "specialized artificial intelligence" and think they are two different things); or misunderstand "specialized" as "weak ability and low level" - it only has a limited scope of application, and it often far surpasses humans in the limited thing (such as AlphaGo playing Go).
fields.典型案例: Let’s look at which AI tools belong to the same batch: AlphaGo (dedicated) that can play Go, AlphaFold (dedicated) that can only predict protein structures, language models for writing articles and chatting (there is controversy, see the depth limit below), and then discuss "why none of them can be regarded as general artificial intelligence."
fields.反例: Think of "specialized" as a derogatory term, thinking that specialized AI means "technically incompetent AI"; or think that "the bigger the model, the more capable it is, and it changes from specialized to universal."
fields.深度上限: We only talk about the distinction between the two types of uses and the comparison of translations, and do not start a debate on the judgment standards in the academic community. There is still debate in the academic community about "whether the large language model is already a general artificial intelligence" (some scholars clearly believe that its technical essence is still a special-purpose AI). This lesson does not draw a conclusion. It only reminds that "the opinions are controversial and there is no generally accepted conclusion."
fields.安全与伦理边界: Don’t believe the “universal” self-declaration in the manufacturer’s slogan, and develop the habit of “asking what a new term refers to when you encounter it.”
fields.教学类比: It’s like seeing a doctor’s expertise: a specialist is very good at treating a certain kind of disease, but for other diseases you have to find another doctor; a general practitioner can look at any disease twice before deciding who to refer it to. The current AIs are almost all “specialists”, and most of them cannot even make “referrals”.
fields.来源依据: People's Daily 2023-06-26 "Pay Attention to the Development of General Artificial Intelligence"; Shanghai University of Finance and Economics Journal (Liu Kai et al., 2018) "Artificial Intelligence Empowers Entrepreneurship: Comparison of Theoretical Frameworks"; for a comparison of homologous translations, see the "Weak Artificial Intelligence" entry in the MBA Think Tank Encyclopedia
fields.通俗解释:
Divide AI according to "wide range of uses" and get these two categories. Specialized artificial intelligence can only use a specific set of algorithms to complete specific tasks, such as AlphaGo, which only plays Go, and AlphaFold, which only predicts protein structures; general artificial intelligence, which has the ability to transfer knowledge, can draw inferences from one instance and draw parallels, and will use its knowledge to solve new tasks - this type has not been realized yet.
It’s easy to get confused in two ways: First, “narrow artificial intelligence” and “dedicated artificial intelligence” are different translations of the same concept, so don’t treat them as two categories; second, “dedicated” is not a derogatory connotation, but its scope is limited, and it often far surpasses humans in the limited things.
It's like seeing a doctor's expertise: a specialist can treat one disease very well, and for other diseases you have to find another doctor; a general practitioner can treat all diseases twice. Today’s AIs are almost all specialist doctors, and most of them cannot even make “referrals”. Whether a large language model is considered universal or not is controversial in academic circles and there is no generally accepted conclusion. When manufacturers advertise “universal”, ask first what they mean.

fields.精确定义: Facts or observations recorded in the form of symbols, numbers, text, images, sounds, etc. are the raw materials for calculation and modeling.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "data naturally equals facts or truth" (data may be wrong, biased, or out of date).
fields.典型案例: Class height record sheet; a class recording.
fields.反例: Treat an unverified rumor as data.
fields.深度上限: It only makes observations of "finding data and classifying types", and does not talk about encoding and storage.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Before collecting data, ask "whether it is necessary and whether it involves personal information."
fields.通俗解释:
Data is the raw material that records observed things and measured results using symbols. It can be numbers, text, photos, or recordings. The class height record sheet is data, and a classroom recording is also data. They are the raw materials for calculation and modeling, like the bricks and stones that are prepared before building a house.
Don’t get confused: data does not automatically equal truth. Records will be wrong, samples will be biased, and content will be out of date. When you get the data, ask three questions: is it accurate, is it complete, and is it new? An unverified rumor looks like news and cannot be counted as data.
Before starting to collect it, develop a habit: first think about whether the data is needed and whether it will involve other people's personal information. Ask this step in front of you, and you will be more confident when you use it later.

fields.精确定义: Data that is organized and contextualized to make sense.
fields.常见误解: Confusing "data" with "information" and treating raw records directly as meaningful conclusions.
fields.典型案例: A string of body temperature numbers is data; sorting by date and marking the higher values is information.
fields.反例: Treat the unorganized original table directly as the conclusion.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "adding context to make sense", not information theory.
fields.通俗解释:
There is a series of body temperature numbers lying there, and there is no way to tell; if you arrange them by date, and then mark which days are higher, your physical condition will be clear at a glance. The former is data and the latter is information. Data is like a handful of scattered beads, and information is like a worn necklace—the beads are still those beads that only look good when they are strung together.
The difference between the two lies in "organization" and "context". Information is data that has been organized and contextualized, making it meaningful to people. The same numbers, arranged in a mess, are data, and when sorted out, they become information.
An easy mistake is to directly regard the original records as conclusions. Making judgments before the table is sorted out is almost like not looking at it. Let me first ask: Do these numbers have context? Only then can we talk about understanding anything.

fields.精确定义: A collection of information that has been organized, verified, and can be used for reasoning or decision-making, such as rules, relationships, and experience summaries.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "more data means more knowledge" (data lacking organization and verification does not constitute knowledge).
fields.典型案例: "Water boils at 100°C at standard atmospheric pressure" is reusable knowledge.
fields.反例: Treat the list of search results as knowledge.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "organizing + verification + usability", not the theory of knowledge.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Knowledge needs to be verified from its source, and AI-generated content cannot replace source verification (Master Version §8.4).
fields.通俗解释:
Information goes one step further and reaches knowledge: information is organized and verified, and turned into a complete set of content that can be used for reasoning and making decisions, including rules, relationships, and experience summaries. "Water boils at 100°C under standard atmospheric pressure" is such a statement. Remember it and it will be useful for boiling water and doing experiments.
To judge whether it is knowledge, look at three things: whether it has been organized, whether it has been verified, and whether it can be used. Information is like parts piled on the table, and knowledge is like a set of things packed into a toolbox and used at any time. An unorganized list of search results is just a collection of information. Don’t treat it as knowledge.
One more thing to remember: knowledge must be verified from its source. No matter how fluent the content generated by AI is, it cannot replace you in reading the original source.

fields.精确定义: A batch of data organized in a unified format for a specific purpose is the basic unit of training and evaluation.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "a random collection of data is a data set" (it needs to have clear scope, format and labeling specifications).
fields.典型案例: A batch of pictures labeled "cat/dog"; a standardized score sheet.
fields.反例: Use photos with messy styles and different formats directly as training data.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "scope + format + purpose", not the collection project.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Data sets must not contain unauthorized personal information and copyrighted material.
fields.通俗解释:
A data set is not a bunch of data collected randomly, it is a batch of data organized in a uniform format for a specific purpose. For example, to train AI to recognize cats and dogs, you need to have a batch of pictures, each labeled as cat or dog, with a unified format and clear scope; a standardized score sheet also counts. Training and evaluation models use such sets of data.
It pays attention to three things: clear scope, unified format, and clear purpose. It's like a book neatly bound according to columns, with pages matching each other. Photos with messy styles and various formats are piled up directly. At best, they can be regarded as a pile of materials, but they cannot be used as a data set.
There is also a bottom line when it comes to group data sets: unauthorized personal information and copyrighted materials cannot be placed in it.

fields.精确定义: Adding labels or descriptions to the data (such as labeling the picture "cat") makes the data available for supervised learning; the label is the target answer or category attached to the sample.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "labeling is just simple manual work and has nothing to do with quality"; or the misunderstanding is that "labeling is the data itself".
fields.典型案例: Mark emails as "junk/normal"; frame pictures as "pedestrian".
fields.反例: The same person labels similar pictures with "cat" and "animal" for one moment, resulting in inconsistent data.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "people have to give examples of answers" and does not talk about the standard system of annotation.
fields.安全与伦理边界: When annotating content involving people, you must pay attention to privacy and respect, and do not use other people's photos for irrelevant exercises.
fields.通俗解释:
In order for the model to learn to give answers from examples, someone must first provide a standard answer for each piece of data. Adding labels or descriptions to data is data annotation: whether emails are marked as "junk" or "normal", pedestrians are framed in pictures, and "cats" are marked on pictures. The label is the target answer or category attached to each sample. It is not the data itself, but an additional answer attached.
Annotation may seem like manual labor, but quality is actually very important. The same person would label similar pictures as "cat" and "animal" at another time. The labels are contradictory and the model will get confused after learning. Only by being serious and consistent can the labeling stand.
You should be more careful when marking content that involves people: don’t do irrelevant exercises with other people’s photos, privacy and respect must be taken into account.

fields.精确定义: The training set is used to adjust model parameters; the validation set is used to adjust settings and select versions during training; the test set is used for final evaluation and must be strictly separated from the training data.
fields.常见误解: Confusing the validation set and the test set; misunderstanding that "the test set can participate in training" (will lead to evaluation distortion, which is a data leak).
fields.典型案例: The analogy of "textbook examples - after-class exercises - final exam papers".
fields.反例: Use the test questions as practice questions and practice over and over again, and then take the full score as your true level.
fields.深度上限: Only role differentiation and simple analogies are done, and division ratios and cross-validation are not discussed.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The evaluation must use data that the model has not seen, otherwise it will amount to false advertising of results.
fields.教学类比: Textbook example questions = training set, exercises = verification set, closed examination papers = test set; but it should be noted that in real life, the division is completed by the program.
fields.通俗解释:
For model learning techniques, the data used must be divided into three pools, each dealing with one section. The training set is textbook example questions, which the model relies on to adjust parameters over and over again; the verification set is an after-class exercise, which is used to test the heat, adjust settings, and choose versions during training; the test set is a closed examination paper at the end of the semester, specifically used to score the total score.
The test paper has an iron rule: it must be strictly separated from the training data, and the model cannot be seen in advance. Taking the test questions as exercises and doing them over and over again, and then taking the test as a perfect score will be regarded as the real level. This is called data leakage, and the results are false. Don’t mix up the verification set and the test set: exercises can be done repeatedly to help adjust the method, but the test paper can only be taken one last time.
It's like taking a class: the example questions will teach you, the exercises will help you find the method, and the final exam paper will reveal the real chapter. In real model training, these divisions do not require human intervention, and the program automatically completes them. The same goes for evaluation. Only by using data that the model has never seen can the results be convincing.

fields.精确定义: Structured data is organized in fixed fields and formats to facilitate direct query (such as tables); unstructured data does not have fixed field formats (such as free text, pictures, audio, and video).
fields.常见误解: Misunderstood as "structured = more advanced data"; or "unstructured data cannot be used".
fields.典型案例: Score sheets (structured) and class recordings (unstructured).
fields.反例: Mixing the two types of data together does not explain the difference in format.
fields.深度上限: It only does identification and classification, not database paradigm.
fields.通俗解释:
The score sheet is filled out neatly, with names, student numbers, and scores assigned to each one. It is clear at a glance that this is structured data—organized according to fixed fields and formats, making it easy to query directly. What about class recordings? The content has no fixed format and can be said wherever you think. This is called unstructured data. Freely written text, pictures, audio, and videos mostly fall into this category.
The two types of data are like two kinds of storage: one is a storage box with divided compartments, the same compartment; the other is a whole bag of things without compartments, which can be packed in different ways. No one is more advanced than others. Unstructured ones can still be used. Don’t think that “structured” means you are superior to others, and don’t think that unstructured ones can’t be used.
When you want to use it, first identify which type you have and explain the format differences clearly. If they are mixed together and dealt with in a dull manner, it is easy to cause trouble.

fields.精确定义: Data quality refers to the extent to which data meets usage requirements in terms of accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, representativeness, etc.; cleaning refers to processing missing, duplicate, errors, and format inconsistencies to make them usable.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the more data, the higher the quality"; the misunderstanding is that "cleaning means deleting data" (also including completion, correction, and unified format).
fields.典型案例: I found that the year of birth in the form was written as "2105" and needed to be checked and corrected.
fields.反例: Ignore the large number of blank cells and calculate the average directly.
fields.深度上限: It only focuses on "finding the problem and explaining why it needs to be fixed" and does not talk about the cleaning algorithm.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The basis for deleting data must be explained, and it must not be tampered with for the sake of “looking good”.
fields.通俗解释:
Whether the data is useful or not depends on several things: whether it is accurate, incomplete, consistent, inconsistent, new, and whether it can represent the real situation. The degree to which this meets the usage requirements is called data quality. In the form, someone's birth year is written as "2105". This is a quality problem and needs to be checked and corrected.
Fixing the problems until they are usable is data cleaning. Fill in the missing parts, remove the duplicates, correct the mistakes, and straighten out the inconsistent formats. Don't think that cleaning means deleting data. Deleting is just a small step. Ignoring the large blank spaces in the table and calculating the average directly, the result will definitely be unreliable.
Cleaning is like selecting vegetables before putting them in the pot: wash away the mud, pick off the bad leaves, and arrange the lengths and lengths before the vegetables are ready. There is also a bottom line: you must explain the basis for deleting data, and you cannot do it just to make the numbers look better.

fields.精确定义: Data describing the data, such as when it was taken, author, format, source, license.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "metadata is not important and can be omitted" (metadata is related to traceability, copyright and quality).
fields.典型案例: The shooting time and equipment information recorded in the photo.
fields.反例: After downloading the material, the source information is deleted, resulting in the inability to be signed.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "data describing data" and its uses, not metadata standards.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Metadata is the basis for copyright and source tracing.
fields.来源依据: NIST AI RMF (requires recording of dataset metadata and characteristics)
fields.通俗解释:
In addition to the picture itself, the photo file also contains a bunch of small information: when it was taken, what equipment was used, who the author is, what format, and where the source is. These data describing the data are called metadata. Time of shooting, author, format, source, license, are all its contents.
It is like an ID card for data: it is not the data itself, but it clearly explains who the data belongs to and where it comes from. Without it, the data will be unclear. When you download materials from the Internet and delete the source information, you will not be able to sign the original author when you look back. This is the price of losing metadata. It relies on it to trace the source of the data, who owns the copyright, and whether the quality is good or not.
There are two good habits: don’t erase the metadata when you get someone else’s files; organize the data yourself and remember the source and permission clearly.

fields.精确定义: Due to improper data collection, labeling, or selection methods, the data cannot fairly and accurately represent the real situation, resulting in systematic deviations in model output.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "deviations are just technical faults" (often stemming from social history and collection design); or "the data is objective so there is no bias".
fields.典型案例: Most of the training photos are during the day, and the model has poor recognition performance at night.
fields.反例: Think of "we have collected a lot of data" as "the data is not biased."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "many examples do not mean they are complete" and does not talk about statistical fairness indicators.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Bias can lead to injustice against specific groups and needs to be identified and addressed.
fields.来源依据: NIST AI RMF (dataset may contain harmful bias or quality issues)
fields.通俗解释:
Most of the training photos were taken during the day, and the model becomes frightened when it comes to recognizing things at night. The fault is not in the algorithm, but in the data: the methods of collection, labeling or selection are inappropriate, the data does not fairly and accurately represent the real situation, and the model's output is overall off track. This is data bias.
It's like scooping soup to judge whether the whole pot is salty or not. If the spoon always scoops from the same corner, the taste will be incalculable. Two common sentences need to be corrected: one is "We have a lot of data, there will be no bias", large quantity does not mean representativeness; the other is "the data is so objective, where does the bias come from", bias often comes from the legacy of social history and loopholes in the collection design, and is not a simple technical fault.
Deviations may also cause certain groups to suffer hidden disadvantages. If they are found, they must be pointed out and how to deal with them must be explained clearly.

fields.精确定义: Data source refers to the original source of the data and its traceable information (collection method, time, institution, authorization status); data rights refers to the rights that individuals have to know, access, correct, delete, and portability of their data.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "data on the Internet can be used at will"; or "data rights only belong to the enterprise or platform".
fields.典型案例: When citing online images, please check the authorization and signature requirements.
fields.反例: Put photos you find online directly into your public works.
fields.深度上限: We only make judgments about "whether it can be used and whether it is necessary to indicate it," without going into the details of legal provisions.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Students' real identities, voices, portraits, locations and other information may not be collected, uploaded or disclosed without authorization.
fields.来源依据: China's "Personal Information Protection Law" and "Data Security Law" (secondary verification before finalizing the specific clauses)
fields.通俗解释:
If I find a photo online, can I put it directly into my public works? Most of the time not. Before using it, you should check its origin: where it originally came from, how it was collected, when, what institution, and what the authorization status is. This traceable origin information is the source of data.
At the other end of the spectrum are data rights. For your own data, you have the right to know who is using it, the right to view it, the right to correct it, the right to delete it, and you can also take it with you to another location. These rights belong to individuals, not just to companies or platforms. Your data is like your personal belongings. Who can move it? You have to nod if you say hello before moving it.
Remember a fact: without authorization, information such as other people’s true identity, voice, portrait, and location cannot be collected, uploaded, or disclosed. When quoting images from the Internet, first check the authorization and signature requirements.

fields.精确定义: Using the network structure of "entity-relationship-entity" to organize knowledge, the knowledge can be queried and reasoned by machines.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "knowledge graph is just a pile of data" (the core is the clear relationship structure between entities).
fields.典型案例: A triplet network such as "Beijing - is - the capital of China".
fields.反例: A bunch of disconnected documents are called a knowledge graph.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "connecting with relationships" and does not talk about graph databases and inference algorithms.
fields.来源依据: Popular content for knowledge engineering; GraphRAG (Microsoft, 2024) for its modern application
fields.通俗解释:
Breaking knowledge into dots and then connecting them using relationships is how the knowledge graph is organized. "Beijing" is an entity, and "Capital of China" is also an entity. Use "is" to connect them in the middle, and a piece of knowledge is included. Thousands of such connections are woven into a network, and machines can query and reason by following the relationships.
It is like a subway line map: stations are entities and lines are relationships. Follow the line one stop at a time and you can find it wherever you go. It's another thing to pile up information - documents are put into folders, and no one knows each other.
To judge whether it is a knowledge graph, just look at one thing: whether the relationships between entities are clearly connected. A pile of data without a relational structure doesn't matter no matter how big it is.

fields.精确定义: The process of finding relevant content from a data collection based on query requirements.
fields.常见误解: Confusing "retrieval" and "generation" (retrieval is responsible for finding, generation is responsible for writing).
fields.典型案例: Find relevant passages in the information package based on keywords and semantics.
fields.反例: You think that AI answers are all "remembered" from memory, but in fact they are retrieved first.
fields.深度上限: It only does "finding" and "judging whether the finding is accurate", and does not talk about the index structure.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The source must be indicated when citing search results.
fields.来源依据: General information retrieval content (including search engine principles)
fields.通俗解释:
Take the query requirements and find relevant content in a batch of data. This process of finding is called retrieval. For example, before AI answers a question, it first takes your question and selects relevant passages in the data package based on keywords and semantics. This step is retrieval.
It is necessary to distinguish two processes: retrieval is responsible for finding, and generation is responsible for writing. Searching means searching through existing information, and writing means organizing the found materials into words. Some people think that AI's answers are all remembered from "memory". In fact, many times it searches first and then answers. If it finds the wrong information, no matter how smoothly it writes, it will be in vain.
It's like going to the library to borrow books: you report your needs, and the administrator takes out the relevant books, instead of moving the entire library to you. One more thing, don’t forget, the search results are quoted in the answer, and the source must be indicated.

fields.精确定义: An inspection process to determine whether the data comes from reliable sources, is traceable, and is suitable for the current task.
fields.常见误解: Treat "fluent speaking and beautiful layout" as credible; treat multiple retweets as multiple sources (actually the same source).
fields.典型案例: Comparing the official notice and self-media reports, it was found that the key figures were inconsistent.
fields.反例: Directly quote the "references" generated by AI.
fields.深度上限: It only trains the method of "looking at the source, comparing the source, and finding the original source" without mentioning the professional standards of journalism.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Citing AI-generated content is not a substitute for source verification (Master §8.4).
fields.来源依据: Master §8.4 Information sources and manual review
fields.通俗解释:
Once you get a piece of information, don’t rush to believe it. Check three things: Is it from a reliable source? Can you follow it back to the original source? Is it relevant to the matter at hand? This set of inspections is data verification and information source judgment.
Don't step on these two pitfalls. One is to look at the packaging: smooth writing and beautiful layout do not mean that the content is credible. The other is to count reposts: the same article has been retweeted five times. It looks like it comes from five sources, but it is actually the same thing. The reliable approach is to look at the source, compare sources, and find the original source. When the official notice and the self-media report were compared, the key figures did not match, and the problem became apparent.
Checking the source is a bit like checking the courier tracking number. Only when you can trace it all the way to the shipper can it be considered reliable. Be especially careful with the "references" generated by AI. They look impressive and it is most dangerous to quote them directly. AI can help, but it cannot replace your own checking.

fields.精确定义: A representation method that maps text, pictures and other data into numerical vectors, so that objects with similar content are closer in the vector space, making calculation and retrieval easier. Semantically similar content can be retrieved according to vector distance - this is the basis of retrieval enhanced generation (RAG) and recommendation systems.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "embedding is to compress the data and make it smaller" (the focus is to make the semantic relationship can be numerically calculated); or it is thought that the vector itself can be directly read by people.
fields.典型案例: "Mobile phone" and "smartphone" are relatively close in vector space.
fields.反例: I thought that the search could only rely on the exact same words.
fields.深度上限: We only talk about the intuition of "near meaning → close distance", and do not talk about vector dimensions and model training.
fields.教学类比: For example, places on a map are placed according to "similarity", but the coordinates are calculated by a program, not drawn by humans.
fields.来源依据: Master §3.1 K2 “How information is represented”; embedded as RAG basis
fields.通俗解释:
Contents such as text and pictures can be converted by the program into a series of numerical values, that is, vectors. Content with similar meanings has calculated vectors that are close to each other. "Mobile phone" and "smartphone" are such a pair of close neighbors. Depending on the distance, content with similar semantics can be retrieved. This is the basis for search enhancement generation and recommendation systems.
It's a bit like a map: places are arranged in order of proximity, and those that are close together are together. The difference is that the coordinates are calculated by a program, not drawn by humans, and humans cannot read the numbers themselves. The vectors are not for you to see.
Two misunderstandings can be solved easily: embedding is not about compressing data and making it smaller, but the focus is on making semantic relationships countable by numbers; retrieval does not require word-by-word matching, as long as the meaning is close enough to be found.

fields.精确定义: The ability to obtain, identify, use and create information in a digital environment, including judgment of information sources, selection and safe use of tools.
fields.常见误解: Equating "being able to use a certain app" with "being digitally literate"; ignoring the judgment of the authenticity of information and the risks of tools.
fields.典型案例: When faced with an AI-generated short video, first check the source before deciding whether to forward it.
fields.反例: When you see a lot of likes, you consider it trustworthy.
fields.深度上限: It only teaches judgment actions directly related to learning and life, and does not expand into a complete media literacy course.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Emphasize "verify first before disseminating" and do not create information panic.
fields.来源依据: UNESCO "Global Digital Literacy Framework"; Master §3.1 K2 "Data Verification"
fields.通俗解释:
If you can use a mobile phone and browse apps, does that count as digital literacy? Not even close. It is a set of abilities to obtain information, distinguish true from false, use tools smoothly, and create in a digital environment. This includes judging where the information comes from and whether it is trustworthy, as well as choosing the right tools and using them safely.
The scenario is very specific: you come across an AI-generated short video, check the source first, and then decide whether to forward it or not. This is where literacy comes into play. On the other hand, if you see a lot of likes, you will believe it and repost it, and the judgment link will be broken.
This skill is like taking care of yourself in the digital world: finding things, distinguishing authenticity from fakes, using tools, and preventing risks, you have to be good at everything. Usually, you should do an extra step of "verify first, then disseminate", and ask more "Is this tool safe and suitable?", and you will get better with practice.

fields.精确定义: The platform continues to push similar content based on user behavior, so that users are only exposed to information that is consistent with their own preferences for a long time, forming an information environment where "the more you look, the narrower you get."
