fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
Most AIs live on the screen, input text and pictures, and output text and pictures. Embodied intelligence is different: it drives physical entities such as robots to perceive and act in the real world, using sensors to see and hear, and using the body to operate. This is what physics AI is talking about.
You can think of it as "putting a body on AI": from communicating through a screen to standing and working directly in the physical world.
There is a big difference between the real world and the screen: objects have weight, movements have friction, and the environment changes at any time. It is much more difficult to perceive accurately and move correctly in such a place than AI in pure software. This is the importance of the word "embodied": intelligence has a body and must directly deal with the physical world.

fields.精确定义: A category of AI models capable of generating new content such as text, images, audio, videos, etc., whose output is based on learning the distribution of training data.
fields.常见误解: It is misunderstood that "generation means copying and pasting existing content" (usually a recombinant generation of a training distribution); or it is misunderstood that the generated content is naturally true and original.
fields.典型案例: Enter a sentence to generate an illustration or a piece of text.
fields.反例: It is believed that the generated content must be accurate and original.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "what can be generated" and what must be verified, not probability and sampling.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The generated content may involve copyright and factual errors, which must be checked and explained before use.
fields.通俗解释:
Generative AI is a type of AI that can "create new things": give it a sentence, and it can write an article, draw an illustration, or create an audio or video. It does not bring you ready-made products from the warehouse, but learns the general appearance of the content from a large number of training materials, and then reorganizes new content that has never appeared before according to this appearance.
This is different from copying and pasting. The model learns the rules in a large amount of materials, and the output is recombined according to these rules; because of this, the things it creates are not guaranteed to be accurate or original, and may bring out incorrect content smoothly.
You can think of it like a painter who has seen countless paintings: the paintings he draws are new, but the method comes from the paintings he has seen. Whether the paintings are true or not has to be checked separately. Use it to generate things, check it before handing it over. This is the bottom line for using this type of tool.

fields.精确定义: Text, images, audio and video and other content generated and output by the AI system.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "AIGC has no copyright issues" (involving training data source, copyright and authorship disputes).
fields.典型案例: Class meeting posters and speeches generated with AI.
fields.反例: Sign the AI-generated content directly as your own original work.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "this is AI-generated content and needs to be marked and verified" and does not talk about the details of legal determination.
fields.安全与伦理边界: When using AI to generate content, you need to explain the source, verify facts, and respect the rights of others.
fields.来源依据: Master §3.2 Concept Example; China's "Measures for Labeling of Synthetic Content Generated by Artificial Intelligence" (2025)
fields.通俗解释:
AIGC refers to the content generated and output by AI: a piece of text, a picture, a piece of audio or video, as long as the finished product is made by AI, it is all under this name. Using AI to make a poster and write a speech for a class meeting are typical AIGC.
There is a point that is often overlooked: you cannot default to "AIGC has no copyright issues". Where the AI ​​training materials come from and who owns the signature of the finished product are still controversial. It is a typical practice to put one's name directly on something generated by AI and regard it as original.
There are two safe ways to use it: first, indicate in the work which parts are generated or participated by AI, and second, check the content yourself before publishing. In this way, you respect other people's right to know, and you don't have to bear unexplainable responsibilities yourself.

fields.精确定义: A model with a large number of parameters, trained on large amounts of text to predict the next unit in a sequence, enabling it to generate and transform language.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "LLM understands language and knows facts" (it is generated based on statistical rules and may produce false content).
fields.典型案例: A conversational model that continues, rewrites, translates, or summarizes text.
fields.反例: Assuming that a model knows something is true just because it describes it convincingly.
fields.深度上限: We only talk about the intuition of "predicting the next word", not the Transformer architecture and attention mechanism.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Models may generate false information, and facts must be checked manually.
fields.教学类比: Think of a highly practiced autocomplete system that predicts what comes next from the preceding text. The analogy does not imply human understanding or intentions.
fields.通俗解释:
A large language model (LLM) learns to predict what comes next in a sequence of text. Given some preceding text, it generates a continuation one unit at a time. After training on large amounts of text, those continuations can take the form of an article, an answer, or a conversation.
This capability supports many language tasks: continuing a passage, rewriting, translating, summarizing, and answering in a chat.
A fluent response is not proof that the model knows a claim is true. It generates text from learned statistical patterns and may produce false information. Moving from “that sounds convincing” to “that is correct” still requires checking.

fields.精确定义: Before the model is "on the job", it first learns for a long time on massive text, image and other data, and masters the laws of language and common sense of the world. This stage of laying the foundation is called pre-training. It takes the longest and is the most expensive, and determines the "foundation" of the model - the scale, quality and coverage of the training data, which directly determines the model's capabilities and deviations.
fields.常见误解: They think that pre-training is "storing knowledge one by one"; they confuse pre-training with subsequent fine-tuning.
fields.典型案例: Understand "why the big model seems to know a little bit of everything" - because it has seen a huge amount of material in the pre-training stage.
fields.反例: Thinking that "you won't know it if you haven't been taught it", it can still combine answers regardless of content it has never seen before (and therefore make mistakes).
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the functions and scenarios of "laying the foundation, consuming resources, and setting the foundation", and does not talk about the training algorithm and data pipeline.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The source and copyright of pre-training data are important points of dispute, which can lead to K6.
fields.教学类比: It’s like the common sense that children have accumulated in daily life before they go to school - they are not taught specifically, but they are seen a lot.
fields.来源依据: A general overview of pre-training-fine-tuning paradigms
fields.通俗解释:
Pre-training is the foundation stage before the model is "on the job": first, study for a long time on massive texts, images and other materials, and get a rough idea of the laws of language and common sense of the world. This is the most time-consuming and expensive step in the entire process. Whether the model is good or not depends entirely on the scale, quality and coverage of the data fed in this step.
It's like what children see and hear in life before going to school: no one has ever taught them step by step. It's more visible and common sense is naturally accumulated. This just explains "why the big model seems to know a little bit about everything" - he has seen a lot of material.
Two things that are easy to confuse: pre-training is not about storing knowledge into a warehouse one by one, and the model is never "knowledgeable without being taught". It can combine the content it has seen to answer new questions. If the combination is wrong, it will still make mistakes; in addition, pre-training is to lay the foundation, which is different from the targeted fine-tuning later, so don't mix them together.

fields.精确定义: After pre-training, another round of training is performed with smaller-scale, more targeted data, so that the model can learn to "understand instructions, answer in a format, and adapt to a certain field." This is fine-tuning; the method of specifically teaching it to "understand human speech" is called instruction fine-tuning.
fields.常见误解: They think that fine-tuning is "retraining from scratch"; or they think that fine-tuning can add knowledge that the model does not originally have out of thin air.
fields.典型案例: Explain "why the same base model can be used as both a customer service assistant and a coding assistant" - relying on different fine-tuning.
fields.反例: Think of "changing the system prompt word" as "fine-tuning".
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the value of "teaching it to be obedient and adapt to the scene", but does not talk about the training details and parameter adjustment methods.
fields.教学类比: Just like the same newcomer, after being trained in different positions, he becomes a customer service or programmer.
fields.通俗解释:
Once the foundation of the model is laid, it needs on-the-job training. This step is called fine-tuning: another round of training with a small batch of more targeted data, so that it can learn to understand instructions, answer in a format, and adapt to a specific field. Among them, the one specifically taught to "understand human speech" is called command fine-tuning.
The same base model can be transformed into different roles if the training direction is different: being transferred to be a customer service assistant is a process of training, and being transferred to be a code assistant is another process. This is also the answer to "Why can one model do several jobs?"
There are two misunderstandings that need to be corrected: fine-tuning is not about overthrowing and starting from scratch, it is about modifying the existing foundation; it cannot insert knowledge that the model does not originally have out of thin air. By the way, changing a few system prompt words is not called fine-tuning. It is changing the way of explanation, not re-training.

fields.精确定义: On the basis of the model's already capable capabilities, it can further guide its behavior to "be consistent with human values and expectations" - such as being more honest, safer, and less harmful output. Alignment answers "how to do it right", which is different from technical ability.
fields.常见误解: They think that the stronger the ability, the more "right" they will automatically be; or they think that alignment can be completed once and for all.
fields.典型案例: Discuss "Why does the model refuse to do some things even though it can obviously do it?" and understand the separation of capabilities and rules.
fields.反例: Treat "answer politely" as "already aligned."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the goals and difficulties of "making behavior meet human expectations", and does not talk about the specific alignment algorithm.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Alignment involves the fundamental question of "whose values", which must lead to the discussion of value alignment in K6.
fields.教学类比: It's like setting rules for a very capable employee: he can do it, but the company requires him not to do everything.
fields.通俗解释:
After the model has the ability, the next step is to guide its behavior toward human expectations: more honest, safer, and less harmful output. This step is called alignment. It answers "what should be done right", which is two different lines from the level of ability.
For example, if there is a very capable employee in the company, the company still has to set rules: just because you can do it, doesn't mean you can do everything. If you ask the model to do something and it refuses to do it, most of the time it’s not that it doesn’t know how to do it, but that the rules are blocking it.
Two common misconceptions: one is that the stronger the ability, the more "right" it is. In fact, ability and compliance are two separate things; the other is that alignment is regarded as a once-finished job, and once it is adjusted, you don't need to worry about it anymore. There is no one-and-done answer to this matter. In addition, answering politely and courteously does not mean that you are aligned. Attitude and following the rules are two different things.

4-07.name: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) / Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)

fields.精确定义: RLHF uses human preference ranking of model output as a reward signal to adjust model behavior; DPO is a simplified method that uses preference data to directly train model alignment.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "AI knows what is right by itself" (preferences are given by humans).
fields.典型案例: Let people compare two responses to see which is better, and use these comparisons to improve the model.
fields.反例: Think that models are born with courtesy and propriety.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "preferences given by people and preferences learned by models" and does not talk about algorithm derivation.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The annotator's preferences will affect model values, and attention should be paid to representativeness and bias.
fields.来源依据: Ouyang et al. "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback" (2022); Rafailov et al. DPO (2023)
fields.通俗解释:
The problem this method solves is: how to teach people’s tastes to the model. The method is to let people compare the two answers given by the model and tell which one is better. These preference rankings become the basis for adjusting the model. RLHF uses this approach; DPO is a simplified version of it, using preference data to directly train the model, saving steps.
It can be understood in terms of the coach leading the players: the coach may not necessarily go out to play in person, but he can tell which moves are good, and the players will make little changes based on the feedback. DPO is equivalent to letting the coach’s comments directly become training content.
One thing needs to be made clear: the model does not know what is right or good by itself. The standards of good and bad are set by people from beginning to end. The little politeness and propriety it knows are all learned from being compared and selected over and over again. They are not born with it.

fields.精确定义: A software system that receives user input and generates responses through a conversational interface, which can be driven by rules or language models.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "chatbots have emotions or personalities" (its responses are computationally generated and do not contain real emotions).
fields.典型案例: Customer service automatically responds; learning assistant dialogue interface.
fields.反例: Think of "kind tone" as "it really cares about me."
fields.深度上限: We only talk about "conversational interface", not the implementation method.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Do not rely on AI as a substitute for real human relationships, and pay attention to the duration of use and content safety.
fields.通俗解释:
A chatbot is a type of software system: you open a dialog box, you type in it, and it replies, and the interaction is completed in one go. The core is the conversational interface. As for what is behind it, it can be rules or language models.
The automatic response in customer service and the dialogue window of the learning assistant are all common appearances.
What tends to go astray is the emotion: the friendly tone of its words does not mean that it really cares about you; those replies are calculated and have no emotions or personality in them. If you think it "understands you", most of the time it's because you listen to the smooth words as your thoughts. Just use it as a tool. If you ask questions clearly, it will be easier for it to answer. If you expect it to be a close friend, you will be misidentifying the target.

fields.精确定义: The language model processes the basic units of text, usually corresponding to words, subwords or character fragments; the text is divided into Tokens and then encoded and calculated. The Chinese standard translation is "Ci Yuan" (named and recommended by the National Scientific and Technical Terms Approval Committee in March 2026), and the industry is still accustomed to using English Token directly. Note: It means the same English word in different fields as "token" in network security and "token" in blockchain. Do not confuse it.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "Token is a word" (a word may be divided into multiple Tokens).
fields.典型案例: A piece of Chinese text will be cut into several segments and then handed over to the model for processing.
fields.反例: It is thought that the model is processed by "words" or "sentences".
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "the text is cut into small fragments", not the word segmentation algorithm and word list.
fields.来源依据: Announcement of the National Committee for Approval of Scientific and Technical Terms (2026-03-25, giving priority to recommending "word elements"); Master Version §3.4
fields.通俗解释:
When the model reads text, it does not read the entire sentence or paragraph, but first cuts the text into small fragments and then processes them. These small fragments are Tokens, and the standard translation in Chinese is "word elements". A fragment may be a word, or it may be just a section of a word or a few characters. A piece of Chinese text is usually cut into such a pile of fragments and given to the model. It's like cutting the ingredients first and then adding them to the pot. The unit that the pot handles at one time is a small piece, not a whole portion.
Don't treat tokens as synonyms of words: a word may be divided into several tokens, and the model is not calculated by "word" or "sentence".
There is another thing with the same name that you should pay attention to: "token" in network security and "token" in blockchain are both called Token in English, but that is the meaning elsewhere. They just share the same English word with the word element here, so don't mix them together.

fields.精确定义: Prompts are input instructions or information provided to the model by the user or the system to guide the model to produce specific output; prompt engineering is a method and practice that guides the model to produce output that is more in line with the required output by designing and adjusting inputs.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "prompt is a universal spell, and if the wording is slightly different, the results will be completely different"; or "prompt engineering can solve all model limitations" and "prompt engineering is equivalent to programming."
fields.典型案例: Write down the tasks, objects, materials, requirements, and inspection standards clearly and then let the model answer.
fields.反例: Just write "Write a good essay for me" and expect satisfactory results.
fields.深度上限: Prompt words are not regarded as all AI abilities; the length or number of prompt words is not used to indicate the ability level.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Tips may not contain private or unauthorized material of others.
fields.教学类比: It’s like giving a task to a new colleague: the clearer you explain it, the closer it will be to expectations; but giving it clearly doesn’t mean the result will be correct.
fields.来源依据: Master version §6.4 Prompt word scaffolding field specifications; §8.2 Red line
fields.通俗解释:
The prompt is the input given to the model: a sentence you say and a piece of material attached guide it where to answer. The prompt project is to figure out how to design this input so that the model output can better meet your needs.
This is like explaining a task to a new colleague: what is the task, who is it for, what materials are used, what are the requirements, and what standards are checked. The clearer the explanation, the closer the thing he hands back will be to what you want. If you only leave one sentence: "Write a good composition for me", then no wonder the writing is empty.
At the same time, don’t overdo it: it is not a universal spell, and the results may not be earth-shaking if you change the wording; the prompt project cannot solve the limitations of the model itself, let alone programming. Model capability is the foundation, and the tip is to make good use of the foundation. Don’t equate the two.

fields.精确定义: Model or system capabilities that can process or generate multiple types of data (such as text, images, audio, video) simultaneously.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "multimodality = multiple models put together" (emphasis on unified processing of multiple data forms).
fields.典型案例: An assistant that can see pictures, read words, and read aloud.
fields.反例: Call "several independent gadgets strung together" multimodal.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "being able to handle multiple forms of information", not the model architecture.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Images and voices involve portrait and sound rights, and use requires authorization.
fields.通俗解释:
Multimodality refers to the ability to "accept any form": with the same model, text, images, audio, and video can all come in and out, instead of just recognizing text. An assistant can look at pictures, read words, and read aloud. This is multi-modal work.
The focus is on "unified processing": multiple forms of information are digested together and communicated with each other in a set of systems. Take a few small tools, each with a section, and string them together into a chain. That doesn't count. It's just an assembly line, not an integrated capability.
You can think of a person who can listen, speak, read and read. His eyes, ears and mouth are in the same head. He can talk about whatever he sees. If there is a translator on one side and a painter on the other to communicate with each other, it is the cooperation of two groups of people, not the ability of one person alone.

fields.精确定义: The phenomenon in which a model generates content that appears to be reasonably smooth but is actually inaccurate, unfounded, or inconsistent with a given source.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "AI deliberately lied" (an error caused by the generation mechanism, not involving subjective intention).
fields.典型案例: The model created a book that didn't exist and gave it seemingly correct page numbers.
fields.反例: Citing "references" given by AI without verification.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "making mistakes and checking them" and does not talk about the probabilistic details of the generation mechanism.
fields.安全与伦理边界: All facts, data, and references provided by AI must be manually verified before use.
fields.教学类比: Use "serious nonsense" to describe the phenomenon, but it must be stated that this is not intentional.
fields.来源依据: Ji et al. "Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation" (2022); Master §3.1 K4
fields.通俗解释:
Illusion refers to the model's serious nonsense: the content seems to be logical and reasonable, but in fact it is inaccurate, has no basis, or does not match the information given. The important point is: it is not deliberately lying, the model does not have the intention to "lie to you", the error is caused by the fault of the generation process itself.
There is a common situation: when you ask about a book, the model will easily make up a book that does not exist at all, and even the page numbers are clearly marked. The more genuine it is, the easier it is to deceive people.
So when you get the output of AI, don’t be fooled by the smoothness, especially the “references” it provides. Don’t quote it directly without verifying it. The rules for using this kind of tool are simple: it will tell you something wrong, and you are responsible for checking it.

fields.精确定义: The process of checking and comparing generated results against factual, quality, safety and task standards, and explaining the basis for choices.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "it looks good and reads smoothly, which means good results".
fields.典型案例: Let the model give two versions of the plan and compare them one by one to see if requirements are missed and if errors occur.
fields.反例: Directly use the result generated for the first time.
fields.深度上限: It only does "item-by-item comparison and verification according to standards" and does not talk about the design of the evaluation system.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Content involving facts and rights must be verified one by one before being used or published.
fields.来源依据: Master version §2.4 Five categories of performance "evaluation"; §3.2
fields.通俗解释:
When AI is used to work, the results cannot be used immediately. They must be reviewed according to standards: are the facts correct, the quality acceptable, whether there are any safety issues, and whether they meet the task requirements. Compare several more versions with each other, and tell which version you finally selected and why you chose it. This whole set of actions is the comparison and verification of the generated results.
The easiest pit to fall into: just looking at the surface. Smooth reading and beautiful layout do not mean that the content is reliable, and the requirements that should be omitted will still be omitted.
The approach can be like acceptance of delivery: check each item against the original requirements, write down which items are missing or wrong, and let the model change it or change it yourself. It was decided to adopt it in the first version, which is the laziest and most accident-prone usage.

fields.精确定义: The retrieval component first finds relevant content from the external knowledge base, and then the generation component combines these contents to generate an answer structure, which is used to supplement knowledge other than model parameters.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "RAG can make the model no longer make mistakes" (it can reduce hallucinations, but still relies on retrieval quality and generation quality).
fields.典型案例: First find the relevant regulations in the company documents, and then let the model answer accordingly.
fields.反例: I thought that the content found by RAG must be correct and relevant.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the process of "check first and write later", not the implementation and optimization of vector retrieval.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The retrieved information may contain expired or false information, and the source still needs to be verified.
fields.教学类比: Open book exam: first turn through the book to find the relevant passage, and then answer accordingly; however, turning to the wrong page will result in a wrong answer.
fields.来源依据: Lewis et al. "Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks" (NeurIPS 2020)
fields.通俗解释:
The process of retrieval enhancement generation (RAG) is just four words: search first and then write. Before the model answers, the retrieval component first finds relevant content in the external knowledge base, and then the generation component combines the found things to organize the answer. In this way, the model can use knowledge other than training, which is equivalent to giving it a bookshelf for checking and using at any time.
Like an open-book exam: first flip through the book to find the relevant paragraph, and then answer according to the paragraph. The answer will be based on evidence and is more reliable than answering from memory.
But don’t expect it to be error-free: turning the wrong page will result in the wrong answer. If the content found is incorrect or irrelevant, or the final answer is deviated, errors will still creep in. RAG can suppress part of the hallucination, but it cannot suppress all of it. Both what is checked and what is written must be checked again.

fields.精确定义: Let the model answer and give evidence based on specified data, rather than relying solely on the parameter memory formed during training; the knowledge base is a collection that organizes these data for retrieval.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "just give it the data and everything will be fine"; ignoring whether the data itself is sufficient and contradictory.
fields.典型案例: Have the model answer the question based only on the given class convention text.
fields.反例: I think the model also knows the information that is not given.
fields.深度上限: It only makes judgments about "whether the data is sufficient and whether the basis is there", and does not talk about knowledge base engineering.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Do not enter personal information from your profile into unsecured tools.
fields.来源依据: Master §4.3 "Question and answer solution based on specified data"
fields.通俗解释:
The method of doing this is to delineate a batch of designated data for the model, require it to answer only based on this batch of data, and show the evidence, and not allow it to freely use the memory accumulated during training. This collection of information is organized for easy retrieval and is called a knowledge base. For example, ask your assistant to report only based on the documents on your desk, and you are not allowed to speak based on your own impressions.
For example, if the model is asked to answer questions based only on the text of the class convention, it must be stated which convention the answer comes from.
Just because the information is given does not mean it is stable. You have to check two things yourself: whether the information is enough, and whether there are any conflicts between the several information. Don’t think that it knows even if it is not provided. The model should not have a say in the materials that are not provided. The measure of judgment lies in these two sentences: whether the data is sufficient and whether the basis is there.

fields.精确定义: During the generation process, the model requests to call external programs or interfaces (such as calculators, searches, databases) according to the agreed format to complete tasks that it cannot directly handle.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the model executes the tool itself" (the model only generates call requests, and the actual execution is completed by an external program).
fields.典型案例: When precise calculations are required, the model requests a calculation procedure.
fields.反例: I thought the model would be able to accurately calculate complex calculations on its own.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "AI can ask external programs for help", not API programming.
fields.安全与伦理边界: What the tool can do is set by people, and people are responsible for the permissions and consequences.
fields.通俗解释:
Tool calling means: you can ask external programs for help when working on the model. When it encounters tasks that it is not good at, such as calculations that need to be calculated accurately, the latest information needs to be checked, or databases need to be browsed, it will issue a call request according to the agreed format and let external programs such as calculators, searches, and databases take over.
The key is to distinguish who will do the work: the model is only responsible for "making requests", and what is actually executed is the external program. After running, the results are handed back, and the model continues to answer. The hands are extended by others, and the mouth belongs to the model.
If you rely on the model to calculate complex calculations accurately, something will probably go wrong. The safest way is to let it call the calculation program. This is like asking an expert to do something: you state your needs clearly, let the expert do the work, and get the results back for later use.

fields.精确定义: Systems that can autonomously call tools, decompose tasks, and perform operations according to multi-step processes under set goals are usually driven by large language models and combined with external tools.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "intelligent agents are autonomous conscious entities" (its autonomy refers to process orchestration and tool invocation in the engineering sense).
fields.典型案例: After receiving "organize this week's notices and generate reminders", search, summarize, and draft by yourself.
fields.反例: Think of "autoresponders" as agents.
fields.深度上限: The focus is on goals, steps, tools, failures and manual checkpoints, not on the number of agents or architectural complexity as a representation of advancement.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The higher the autonomy, the more artificial judgment points, stopping conditions and authority boundaries need to be set.
fields.教学类比: It's like an assistant that can run errands by itself, but it has no intentions. Goals and boundaries must be set by people.
fields.来源依据: Master §3.1 K4 "Agent"; §3.4 Unified Boundary; Anthropic "Building effective agents" (2025)
fields.通俗解释:
An AI agent is a system that can advance its work under a given goal: after receiving a task, it will break down the steps, call tools, and execute it step by step according to a multi-step process. It is usually driven by a large language model and equipped with external tools to do it. For example, let it "organize this week's notifications and generate reminders", and it will find, summarize, and draft notifications by itself without having to be urged at every step.
Its autonomy is in the engineering sense: it can arrange processes and adjust tools, but it is not a living creature with self-awareness. It is up to people to decide what the goals are and where to draw the boundaries.
Use this criterion to distinguish: something that can only reply automatically is not called an agent. What we really need to pay attention to is whether its goal is clear, how to break down the steps, what to do if it fails, and whether people have checkpoints. These are more important than "how powerful it is."

fields.精确定义: Multiple processing steps and their data flow relationships organized in a certain sequence to complete a task.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the workflow must be fully automated" (it may also include manual review).
fields.典型案例: The complete process of "finding information→extracting key points→checking→drafting→checking".
fields.反例: If things are lumped into one step, problems cannot be located.
fields.深度上限: We only do step arrangement, branching and rollback design, not production-level process engineering.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Key judgment points in the process must be reviewed by humans.
fields.通俗解释:
Workflow is to arrange the procedures for a task: which steps it is divided into, which step to do first and which step to do next, and how to hand over the results of the previous step to the next step. For example, when dealing with one thing, you can arrange it into: finding information, extracting key points, checking, drafting, and checking, step by step, and the data will be passed down along the process.
It does not require full automation. There can be a manual review step in the process, and the person's review can be reviewed by others.
Breaking down the steps has a real advantage: if there is a problem in any link, you can find out where it is. On the contrary, if everything is done in one big step and done in one go, when the result is wrong, you can’t even tell where the problem is. Arranging steps, setting up branches, and leaving a way back are the basic skills of building a process.

fields.精确定义: Clearly designate the points in the human-AI collaboration process where decisions, verification, or approval must be made by humans. The EU's Artificial Intelligence Act collectively refers to this type of requirement as "human oversight"; the term "human-in-the-loop" often referred to in the field of artificial intelligence is the embodiment of the same idea.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "if the AI passes the inspection, no one needs to look at it"; the "click to agree" is regarded as "it has been carefully verified".
fields.典型案例: Before publishing, people will check the facts and privacy before deciding whether to make it public.
fields.反例: Send the AI-generated list directly without checking.
fields.深度上限: It only makes judgments about "which links must be decided by people" and does not talk about the organizational governance structure.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Decisions involving facts, rights, safety, and public release must be made by humans.
fields.来源依据: Master §2.2 Collaboration and co-creation; §6.3 Third layer of responsibility access control
fields.通俗解释:
When people and AI work together, several links must be circled in the process: these areas must be determined, reviewed, and approved by humans. This pre-specified pass is called a manual judgment point. The EU's Artificial Intelligence Act refers to this requirement collectively as "artificial supervision." The "human in the loop" often said in the field of intelligent agents talks about the same idea.
A typical one: When AI-generated content is to be released publicly, humans must first check the facts and check the privacy, and then the content will be released after the humans nod.
Two misunderstandings need to be broken: First, "AI has checked everything, and people don't need to look at it anymore." The final responsibility for checking always lies with people; second, "clicking on consent means it has been checked." If you click on agree without looking carefully, the check is in name only. The AI-generated list is sent out without even looking at it, and this is often the moment when things turn upside down.

fields.精确定义: A discipline that studies the design and evaluation of interactions between humans and computer systems, focusing on usability, efficiency, experience, and security.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "HCI only cares about whether the interface looks good or not" (it also covers interaction process, understandability and security).
fields.典型案例: Why is it easy for users to use the same function incorrectly if the prompt method is changed?
fields.反例: We only pursue beautiful interfaces but make them incomprehensible.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "whether it's easy to use or not, whether it's easy to understand or not", and it doesn't talk about professional methods of interaction design.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The design should consider the safety and health of minors.
fields.通俗解释:
Human-computer interaction (HCI) is a discipline that studies "how people interact with computers": how to design interaction methods and how to evaluate whether they are effective or not. It focuses on four things: whether it is smooth to use, whether it is efficient, whether the experience is good, and whether it is safe or not.
Don't think that it only cares about the beautiful interface. For the same function, if the prompt method is changed, users will easily use it incorrectly - this type of problem is what HCI is concerned about. If you can't understand it, can't find it, or click on it wrongly, these are all interactive problems.
Think of it like a door handle: if you install a handle on the door, you will know what to pull it at a glance, no need to put a note; if you have to read instructions to open the door, then the design is not done well. The interface is beautiful but difficult to understand and use. In HCI’s opinion, it is a failed design.

fields.精确定义: When using or publishing AI-generated content, state that the content is generated or participated by AI according to specifications, and add identification as required. There are two types of identification: explicit identification is visible to the naked eye (such as corner mark, watermark, text prompt), and implicit identification is a technical mark hidden in the file (such as metadata, digital watermark) for machine identification and traceability.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "if AI is used, no one will know it"; the "marking AI" is regarded as "you don't have to be responsible"; it is believed that "adding a watermark is just a formality" and ignores the value of labeling for the right to know and the traceability of content.
fields.典型案例: In the description of the work, indicate "This picture was generated with the assistance of AI and has been manually modified."
fields.反例: Publish the images generated by AI as real photos; use "if there is no label, it is not generated" as the basis for judgment.
fields.深度上限: We only make judgments about "whether and how to mark", and do not talk about the implementation of marking technology.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Labeling is a requirement of integrity and responsibility, and labeling does not relieve the user of verification and responsibility.
fields.教学类比: Like the ingredient list on food packaging: the visible part tells consumers, while the invisible part is left for regulatory traceability.
fields.来源依据: China's "Measures for Labeling of Synthetic Content Generated by Artificial Intelligence" (effective from September 1, 2025)
fields.通俗解释:
When content is generated with AI or participated in the production, it must be stated according to the specifications that it was made by AI, or what part AI participated in. There are two ways of identification: explicit ones visible to the naked eye, such as corner marks, watermarks, and a line of text prompts; implicit ones hidden in files, such as metadata and digital watermarks for machine identification and traceability.
It's like the ingredient list on a food package: the visible part tells the buyer, while the invisible part is left to the regulator to trace the source.
Some people think that "if you use AI, no one will know about it", or "if you mark it with AI, you don't have to take responsibility", and some think that adding a watermark is just a formality - all three of these are wrong. Marking protects other people’s right to know and allows the content to be traced to its source in the future; you will still be responsible for the parts you are responsible for if marked. Annotating "This picture was generated with AI assistance and has been manually modified" is the simplest and correct approach.

fields.精确定义: It means that the model learns text, images, sounds and other information together from the beginning, and can naturally "understand multiple forms at the same time", instead of adding a picture viewing function to a model that only knows text later.
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "being able to process images" equals "native multi-modality"; ignoring the difference in capabilities between post-processing and native.
fields.典型案例: Compare the difference between "being able to describe pictures" and "being able to speak, look at pictures and respond at the same time" to appreciate the coherence of native multimodality.
fields.反例: Think of "speech-to-text reprocessing" as native multimodality.
fields.深度上限: We only talk about the intuition and benefits of "processing multiple forms uniformly from the bottom", not the encoding and fusion mechanisms.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Multimodality brings new risks such as deepfakes, which can lead to content security.
fields.教学类比: Like the difference between "growing up bilingual" and "memorizing dictionaries when you grow up" - the former is natural integration, the latter is externalization.
fields.来源依据: General discussion of native multimodal models
fields.通俗解释:
Native multimodality means that the model learns text, images, sounds and other information together from the very beginning, and is naturally capable of "understanding multiple forms at the same time", instead of first building a model that only knows text and then plug-in the ability to read pictures to it afterwards.
This difference is like learning a language: for a child who grew up in a bilingual environment, the two languages ​​are integrated in his mind, and he can switch back and forth without any stumbling; when he becomes an adult, he learns it by memorizing a dictionary, and there are more or less traces of "translate first and then understand". The former is native and the latter is external.
Don’t be biased by the phrase “can process pictures” when making judgments. Being able to see pictures does not mean native multi-modality. A detour like "speech to text and then processing" is an external approach. The advantage of native is coherence: you can read the pictures, talk and respond at the same time, all in one go, rather than a relay of several parts.

fields.精确定义: Context is the information that the model can read simultaneously when generating the current output. There are three sources: user input, previous conversations, and externally retrieved content; the context window is the maximum number of Tokens that the model can process at the same time. The larger the window, the longer the data that can be processed simultaneously (such as an entire book), but the cost is also higher; content beyond the window will be "forgotten".
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "the model remembers all our previous conversations" (most of the context is only valid within a single session); thinking that "the larger the window, the smarter the model is"; equating the window size with "good or bad memory".
fields.典型案例: Explain "why AI will forget what was said before after chatting for too long" - because it exceeds the window; put a long piece of information into the conversation and then ask questions, so that the model can answer based on it.
fields.反例: It is thought that after closing the conversation (or changing the conversation), the model still remembers the content of the last conversation.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the intuition of "how much you can see at one time, you can use it only when you see it, and you will forget it if you exceed it". It does not talk about the attention mechanism and long context expansion technology.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Content put into context may be saved; feeding sensitive information and large amounts of personal data risks leakage.
fields.教学类比: It's like a "desktop" with a limited size: only the information that can be placed can be used for reference. If the table is full, the old ones must be taken away. Once the desktop is cleared, it will not be remembered.
fields.来源依据: Master §3.1 K4 "Prompts and Context"; Long Context Model General Discussion
fields.通俗解释:
Context is the information that the model can see at the same time at the moment when it generates the answer. It comes from three sources: the words you input this time, the content discussed earlier in this round of dialogue, and the information retrieved from the outside. The context window is the maximum number of Tokens that can be installed at one time. The larger the window, the longer the data that can be accommodated, such as an entire book, but the cost will also increase; the part beyond the window will be "forgotten" by the model.
Think of it as a table with a finite size: only the information that can be placed on it is eligible for reference. When the table is full, the old things have to be taken away; when the table is cleared, what was previously placed will not be remembered.
There are a few misunderstandings to clear up: the model does not remember all your previous conversations, and most of them are only valid within a single session. If you close the conversation and open it again, it will not recognize the last chat; a larger window does not mean that the model is smarter, and a larger desktop does not mean that it has a better brain. If you want it to answer based on a long piece of information, put the information into the conversation so that it can be seen and used.

fields.精确定义: Package a reusable "method of doing things" so that the AI can execute it according to this method when needed, instead of reinterpreting it every time. This packaging unit is called a skill. It allows agent capabilities to be installed, shared and combined like plug-ins.
fields.常见误解: Confuse Skill with "system prompt word"; or confuse it with "Learning Method Skill" in the course (different things with the same name).
fields.典型案例: Equip the AI with a "form making" skill package, and it will do it according to fixed specifications when it encounters form tasks in the future.
fields.反例: Say "write more prompt words" as "add a skill".
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the concept and value of "reusable package of work methods" and does not talk about the writing format of skill files.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Installing unsolicited skill packs may pose security risks, leading to API/permissions issues.
fields.教学类比: It's like giving employees a set of "standard operating manuals" and they follow them without having to teach them from scratch every time.
fields.来源依据: The general concept of intelligent engineering in 2025
fields.通俗解释:
A skill package is a package and storage of a method of doing things. When the AI encounters the corresponding task, it will execute it according to this packaged method, without having to explain how to do it every time. This packaged unit is called Skill. It allows the capabilities of intelligent agents to be installed, removed, shared, and combined like plug-ins.
It's like giving an employee a standard work manual: when a job comes, he flips through the manual and follows it, without the need for a master to repeat it all over again. Install a "form making" skill package, and when encountering form tasks in the future, it will follow fixed standards.
Don’t confuse two points: the skill package is not the same as the system prompt word, they are two different things; the “learning method Skill” mentioned in the course is another thing with the same name. Writing a few more prompt words is not called "adding a skill". If it is not packaged into a set of reusable methods, it cannot be called a skill.

fields.精确定义: The intelligent agent does not "question and answer", but operates in a cycle: observe the current situation → think about the next step → execute it → see the results → decide the next step, and so on until the task is completed. This repeated advancement mechanism is the agent cycle.
fields.常见误解: Think of the agent as "a chatbot that replies longer at a time"; ignore it and need to "see the results first and then adjust."
fields.典型案例: Observe an agent that can do a multi-step task: it first checks information, then writes a draft, checks and modifies, and finally submits.
fields.反例: Thinking that "AI can do multi-step tasks at once".
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the cyclic intuition of "observation-action-observation again" and does not talk about cyclic control and engineering implementation.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The longer the loop and the higher the autonomy, the more important the human judgment point becomes.
fields.教学类比: Just like people cooking: take a bite → add salt → taste again → adjust again, instead of closing your eyes and adding all the seasonings at once.
fields.来源依据: General discussion of agent paradigms such as ReAct
fields.通俗解释:
The work of the intelligent agent is not a matter of asking and answering, but advancing in circles: look at the current situation, think about the next step, execute it, see the results, and then decide how to proceed, and continue in circles until the task is completed. This recurring mechanism is called an agent cycle.
Just like a person cooking: take a bite, add a spoonful of salt, taste again, adjust again, adjust the actual situation in the pot while cooking, instead of pouring all the seasonings at once with your eyes closed.
You can understand it if you look at an intelligent agent that can do multi-step tasks: first check the information, write a draft, check back, correct it, and then submit it. After each step, check the results before moving on to the next step. Don’t think of it as a “chatbot with extremely long replies”, the kind of thing that is generated once and then handed in. No one pays attention to the quality in the middle. It is unrealistic to expect AI to do all multi-step tasks correctly in one go. The value of the cycle lies precisely in the fact that mistakes can be discovered and corrected on the spot.

fields.精确定义: "Scaffolding" refers to a complete set of supporting components (tools, memory, process control, etc.) built around the model so that the model can actually work; "sub-agent" refers to the division of large tasks into several small agents with division of labor to complete respectively. Together they answer "What components does an AI application consist of?" This layer of supporting components is also called Harness (can be translated as "control layer") in English, which refers to the same thing.
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "having a strong model means having a useful agent"; ignoring the role of peripheral components.
fields.典型案例: Disassemble a tool that can automatically complete reports: model + tool + memory + process control + checkpoint, and what each part does.
fields.反例: Think of "the model is strong" as "the application must be easy to use".
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the structural intuition of "what components the application consists of", but does not talk about the framework and code implementation.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The more components and permissions there are, the greater the risk, so discussions on permissions and security are required.
fields.教学类比: It's like building a house: the model is an engine, but it also needs wheels, steering wheels, and brakes before the car can go on the road.
fields.来源依据: The general concept of intelligent engineering in 2025
fields.通俗解释:
For a working AI application, a model alone is not enough. The complete set of supporting components built around the model, such as tools, memory, process control, etc., is called scaffolding. It is also called Harness (control layer) in English, which means the same thing. If the task is too large, it can be divided into several small agents with different divisions of labor to complete the tasks separately. These are sub-agents. These two together answer a question: What components does an AI application consist of?
To use an analogy: the model is an engine. The engine alone cannot drive on the road. It also needs wheels, steering wheels, and brakes to make it a car.
It becomes clear when you take apart a tool that automatically writes reports: the model is responsible for thinking, the tool is responsible for checking and writing, the memory manages the previous progress, the process controls the arrangement sequence, and the checkpoints ensure quality. No matter how good the model is, but the finished product is difficult to use, it is mostly because the peripheral components are not set up properly.

fields.精确定义: Let the AI remember important information about you or the task (preferences, habits, things you’ve done before) across conversations and use it next time instead of starting from scratch each time. It's not the same as a "contextual window": the window is the temporary desktop, and the long-term memory is the filing cabinet.
fields.常见误解: Confusing long-term memory with “longer context”; ignoring the privacy risks posed by memory.
fields.典型案例: An assistant remembers your favorite layout style and automatically uses it next time without having to explain it again.
fields.反例: He believes that "AI naturally remembers all conversations."
fields.深度上限: We only talk about the value and privacy cost of "remembering across conversations and understanding you the more you use it", but not about the memory storage mechanism.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The more memories there are, the greater the risk of privacy and "being profiled", so it needs to be linked with privacy protection.
fields.教学类比: For example, there is a filing cabinet on the assistant's desk to remember your preferences; but the contents in the cabinet may also be seen by others.
fields.来源依据: General discussion of agent memory (merging F-B11 and F-D12)
fields.通俗解释:
Long-term memory allows AI to remember important information about you across conversations: preferences, habits, and things you have done before, so that you can use it next time without having to start from scratch every time. For example, the assistant remembers your favorite layout style, and the next time you write something, it will automatically follow that style without you having to mention it.
It is not the same thing as the context window: the window is a temporary desktop, and only the information that can fit in this round of dialogue can be referenced; the long-term memory is a filing cabinet, which will still be there even if the things are put away, another conversation.
Just because you can remember it, you also have to settle the account of privacy: your preferences and habits are stored in the cabinet. Who keeps this information and who can see it is worth paying attention to. In addition, "AI naturally remembers all conversations" is an illusion. Memory is a designed ability, not something that comes by default.

fields.精确定义: "Ambient programming" refers to using natural language to roughly describe what you want, and letting AI write the code directly and modify it while chatting. The threshold is low but the controllability is weak; "Specification-driven programming" means to first clearly write down the requirements, constraints, and acceptance criteria (specifications), and then let AI implement it according to the specifications, which is more controllable and more suitable for formal projects. The two represent "casual" and "rigorous" approaches.
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "atmosphere programming can replace all development"; or thinking that "writing specifications is writing code".
fields.典型案例: Compare the quality difference between "just talk about an idea and let AI implement it" and "write down the requirements and then implement them".
fields.反例: Think of "running" as "getting it right".
fields.深度上限: We only talk about the differences between the two methods and their respective applicable scenarios, and do not talk about development tools and engineering details.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Someone must be responsible for reviewing the code generated by AI, and the responsibility cannot be passed on to the tool.
fields.教学类比: Atmosphere programming is like "do it first and see", and specification programming is like "draw the drawing first and then build it".
fields.来源依据: Popular concepts for AI programming in 2025
fields.通俗解释:
There are two ways to write code with AI. One is called atmosphere programming: use natural language to roughly describe what you want, let AI write it directly, and make changes while chatting. It is quick to get started, has a low threshold, and has weak controllability. The other type is called specification-driven programming: first write the requirements, constraints, and acceptance criteria into clear specifications, and then let AI implement it according to the specifications, which is more controllable and more suitable for serious projects.
One is casual and the other is rigorous, just like decorating a house: the former is done while decorating and looking at what you like, while the latter is based on drawings first and then starting construction, checking and accepting the drawings every step of the way.
How to choose depends on the situation: just try out an idea, atmosphere programming is enough; if it needs to be delivered and maintained for a long time, the specifications must be clearly written before it is stable. Don't believe that "atmosphere programming can cover all development", and don't think of "writing specifications" as writing code. Specifications are drawings of requirements, and codes are implementations. They are two different things. Just because you're running doesn't mean you've done it right. You can't avoid the acceptance criteria.

fields.精确定义: It refers to the ability to ask questions clearly and let AI truly understand what you want. For the same thing, if you explain it vaguely, the AI ​​will give a vague answer. Only by clarifying the background, requirements and format can AI give useful results. This is the first step in "making good use of AI".
fields.常见误解: They believe that "the longer the prompt word is, the better" or "the more polite the AI is, the better the answer will be"; they equate prompt literacy with memorizing conversational skills templates.
fields.典型案例: For the same task, use "Help me write something" and "Help me write a 100-word piece of popular science about kittens for third-grade students to read" to compare the difference in results.
fields.反例: Blame all "AI's poor answers" on AI, and don't reflect on whether you asked clearly or clearly.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the key points of "state the requirements clearly" (background, requirements, format, examples), and does not talk about prompt word techniques and routines.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Prompt literacy is learning ability, and "prompt injection" (attacking security) are two different things, so don't confuse them.
fields.教学类比: Like asking for directions: Saying "How to get there" and saying "I want to go to the train station, what time is it now, and I'm in a hurry" will get completely different help.
fields.通俗解释:
Prompt literacy is the ability to ask questions clearly and let AI truly understand what you want. If the same thing is stated vaguely, the answer will be vague; only if the background, requirements, and format are clearly explained, it will give you something useful. If you want to use AI well, this is the first step.
It's like asking for directions: if you just say "how to go", people won't know where you are going; if you say clearly "I want to go to the train station, what time is it now, are you in a hurry?", you will get completely different instructions. This is the difference in output between asking AI to "help me write something" and "help me write a 100-word piece of popular science about kittens for third-grade students to read."
Two misconceptions need to be corrected: longer prompt words are not better, being polite will not buy good answers, and memorizing conversational skills templates is not considered literacy. When the AI ​​answers poorly, first look back and see if you have asked the question clearly. Don’t put all the blame on the AI.

fields.精确定义: It means that when writing homework and doing research, it is clear which methods of using AI are considered "helping" (such as checking information, organizing ideas, and checking grammar), and which ones are considered "cheating" (such as directly handing in answers generated by AI to pretend to be one's own results). The core is: AI can be used, but it cannot be used to think for you, nor can it be used in secret.
fields.常见误解: They think that "using AI means cheating" (one size fits all); or that "it's okay if it can't be detected anyway".
fields.典型案例: Discuss where to draw the line between "use AI to help me correct wrong sentences" and "let AI finish writing and hand it over directly."
fields.反例: Treat the "results of AI participation" completely as "your own independent results."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the judgment of "which usage is allowed and which is not allowed" and does not discuss the differences in provisions stipulated by each school.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Involving honesty, fairness and respect for the work of others are the most realistic ethical topics for students.
fields.教学类比: It's like using a calculator: it's okay to use it to check calculations, but it's not okay to submit what the calculator calculates as "my calculations."
fields.来源依据: UNESCO Guide to the Use of AI in Education
fields.通俗解释:
When using AI for homework and research, you have to draw clear lines yourself: for things like checking information, organizing ideas, and checking grammar, it's okay to let AI "help"; if you hand over the answers generated by AI directly and pass them off as your own, that's "cheating." There are two core sentences: AI can be used, but it cannot be used to think for you, nor can it be used in secret.
Compare it with a calculator: use it to check your calculations, and there is nothing wrong with it; write "I calculated it" on the calculator and hand it in, and the nature will change.
There are two methods to avoid: one is to treat the use of AI as cheating, and helping and cheating are inherently separate; the other is to rely on the mentality of "it can't be found out anyway", gambling on luck, and losing integrity. The judgment method is very simple: the results of AI participation cannot be completely said to be its own independent results. What is used and where it helps is spread out.

fields.精确定义: It refers to the technology that allows machines to "understand" images and videos: identify what is in the photo (image recognition), recognize who this is (face recognition), and understand the dynamics in the picture (video understanding). It's all behind the automatic beautification of photos taken with a mobile phone, recognition of products by scanning, and unlocking by swiping your face.
fields.常见误解: Think of "automatic photo beauty" as just a filter; or think that "what the machine sees is what people see."
fields.典型案例: Use your mobile phone to scan and identify plants or products, and understand "how the machine recognizes what it is."
fields.反例: I thought that "AI sees pictures exactly the same as humans see pictures."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the intuition of "what machines can understand images and what they can do", and does not talk about technical principles such as convolution and feature extraction.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Facial recognition involves privacy and consent and must be linked to privacy protection (see 6-04).
fields.教学类比: It's like equipping a machine with a pair of "eyes that can recognize things" - but what it sees is not a picture, but a bunch of numbers.
fields.通俗解释:
The technology that allows machines to "understand" images and videos is called computer vision. Its tasks include: recognizing what is in the photo, which is image recognition; recognizing whose face it is, which is face recognition; and understanding what is moving in the picture, which is video understanding. It is responsible for automatically beautifying your face when taking photos with your mobile phone, identifying products by scanning them, and unlocking them by swiping your face.
It's like equipping a machine with a pair of eyes that recognize things, but what these eyes see is not the picture itself, but a bunch of numbers.
So don’t think that “AI reading pictures” is the same as seeing pictures by humans: just because a machine can recognize it accurately doesn’t mean it “sees” like a human being. If you think of automatic beautification when taking photos as just a normal filter, you also underestimate it. It is the machine recognizing your face. Scanning with your mobile phone to recognize what a plant or product is, the recognition behind it is different from the human eye.

fields.精确定义: It refers to allowing the machine to "understand human speech" (speech recognition, converting sounds into text) and "speak" (speech synthesis, converting text into natural sounds). Voice assistants, recording to text, audiobook reading, and navigation broadcasts all use these two technologies.
fields.常见误解: Confusing speech recognition and speech synthesis (one is "listening" and the other is "speaking"); thinking that "the voice assistant really understands the meaning."
fields.典型案例: Say a sentence to the voice assistant and observe the complete process of "listening-understanding-answering-speaking".
fields.反例: I thought that "speech recognition is to record and play the voice."
fields.深度上限: We only talk about the distinction and use of "listening and speaking are two different technologies" and do not talk about acoustic models and signal processing.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Voice cloning may be used for fraud and forgery and must be linked to deep forgery (see 6-06).
fields.教学类比: It's like equipping a machine with "ears" and a "mouth" - the ears are responsible for listening, and the mouth is responsible for speaking. They are two different sets of abilities.
fields.通俗解释:
Machine "listening" and "speaking" are two sets of technologies. Converting words spoken by people into text is called speech recognition, which is to equip the machine with ears; converting text into natural sounds and speaking it is called speech synthesis, which is to equip the machine with a mouth. The recording is converted into text by the ears, and the reading of the audio book and the navigation broadcast are done by the mouth. Each side does its own thing.
Say a sentence to the voice assistant and you will see the complete Solitaire: first listen to what you said clearly, then understand the meaning, organize the answer, and finally synthesize the voice to say it. In this chain, listening and speaking are different skills at both ends.
There are a few assumptions that need to be corrected: Speech recognition is not about recording and playing sounds, it is about turning sounds into text; voice assistants can only "understand" things to the extent that they can "continue to do it." Don't take it as really understanding what you mean. Just remember this sentence: one is listening and the other is speaking, don't get into a mess.

4-33.name: Machine Translation and Natural Language Processing (NLP)

fields.精确定义: Natural language processing (NLP) is a general term for technologies that allow machines to "understand and use human language", including translation, summarization, sentiment analysis, question and answer, etc. Machine translation is one of the most commonly used: automatically converting one language into another. They deal with the most common AI ability of "text".
fields.常见误解: They think "machine translation is looking up a dictionary word by word"; or they think "NLP is translation".
fields.典型案例: Use a translation tool to translate a sentence, compare the machine version and the manual version, and discuss "where machine translation is prone to errors."
fields.反例: I think that "if the translation is smooth, it must be translated correctly."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the intuition of "what machines can process language and what it can do", and does not talk about technical principles such as word vectors and attention.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Translation involves cultural differences and context, so students are reminded that the results need to be checked manually.
fields.教学类比: It's like carrying a "multilingual assistant" with you - but it may only understand the literal meaning and not the underlying meaning.
fields.通俗解释:
Natural language processing (NLP) is a general term for technologies that allow machines to understand and use human language. Translation, summarization, sentiment analysis, and question and answer are all included in it. Machine translation is one of the most commonly used: automatically converting one language into another.
It's like carrying an assistant who knows multiple languages ​​with you: if you throw in a Chinese sentence, the foreign language version will come out immediately. But this assistant may only understand the literal meaning and not the underlying meaning.
Use a translation tool to translate a sentence, and then compare it with the human-translated version. It is easy to see the clue: a smooth translation by a machine does not mean that it is translated correctly. The tone, puns, and connotations in the words are most likely to be distorted. There are two misunderstandings that need to be cleared up: machine translation is not a word-by-word dictionary search; NLP is far more than just translation. Word processing is the most common skill of AI, and translation is only one part of it.

fields.精确定义: It refers to stringing together the AI applications that students come into contact with daily into a map: learning (AI tutoring, taking pictures and solving problems), entertainment (short video recommendations, AI painting, games), life (navigation, shopping recommendations, takeout), information (news push, search, translation), creation (song writing, video making) - to understand "where AI has penetrated and what each is doing."
fields.常见误解: Think "AI is a chatbot"; ignore that AI has already been embedded in various daily products.
fields.典型案例: Make a list of "AI I encountered in a day": from getting up to going to bed, which links actually have AI working behind the scenes.
fields.反例: I thought that "if you haven't used ChatGPT, you haven't been exposed to AI."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the overall impression of "AI is everywhere and what it is doing everywhere" and does not expand on the technical details of each application.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Helping students realize that "they have been affected by AI" is the starting point for media literacy and AI literacy.
fields.教学类比: It's like drawing a "map of electrical appliances in your home" - you think it's just the TV, but in fact the refrigerator, washing machine, and microwave are all working.
fields.来源依据: The “application” dimension of AI4K12/OECD AI literacy framework
fields.通俗解释:
If you put together a picture of the AI applications you encounter in daily life, you will find that they have already covered every corner of life: in learning, there are AI tutors and taking pictures to solve problems; in entertainment, there are short video recommendations, AI painting, and AI in games; in life, there are navigation, shopping recommendations, and takeaways; in terms of information, there are news push, search, and translation; in terms of creativity, they can write songs and make videos. What this map wants to convey is that AI is not far away, but in the various products at your fingertips.
It's like drawing an electrical map of your home: you think only the TV is working, but in fact the refrigerator, washing machine, and microwave oven are working every day.
A way to verify this: Make a list of "AIs I encountered in a day" and go through it from getting up to going to bed. You will find many more than you think. Thinking that "AI is just a chatbot" or "having never used a chat AI means you have never been exposed to AI" are all looking at the map in a narrow way.

fields.精确定义: Low-latency, interruptible voice and AI natural conversation capabilities.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
Real-time voice dialogue refers to a low-latency, interruptible voice communication capability: AI can respond as soon as the voice is spoken, and you can interrupt it at any time, so that there is no interruption. In the past, voice interaction often followed three steps: "you finish speaking, it thinks, and then it responds to you", with waiting in between; real-time dialogue makes these waiting almost insensible.
There are two key points: low latency and quick response; it can interrupt, so it can catch you when you change your words or interrupt, without having to wait for it to finish a whole paragraph.
It's as natural as talking on the phone: the person on the other side can pick up your conversation at any time, and you can grab the conversation at any time. This is the normal way for people to chat with others. Real-time voice dialogue brings this normality between humans and AI.

fields.精确定义: Generate video clips from text or image cues.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
AI-generated video refers to the generation of video clips from text or image prompts: give the AI a text description, and it will produce a short video based on it; or give it a picture, and the picture will be extended from the picture as a starting point to become a video.
The two starting points each have their own explanations: the text is "write it out for you to act", and the image is "take a picture and continue it for you". The methods are different, and the output is all video clips.
It's like making a movie: the text prompt is like adding storyboards to the script, and the machine "shoots" it; the image prompt is like handing over a still, and the machine continues to act. The unit of output is a fragment, not a complete film. What people have to do is to describe clearly what they want, and then select the available parts from the generated results.

fields.精确定义: Generate musical songs from text or audio prompts, including vocals and accompaniment.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
Give the AI a text or audio prompt, and it can generate music songs accordingly. Pay attention to the completeness of the finished product: the generated song includes both vocals and accompaniment. It is a complete song with continuous singing and playing, not a thin melody.
There are two ways of prompting: the text prompt is "Describe the song you want", and the audio prompt is "Use a ready-made sound as a basis." Both paths ultimately lead to the same kind of output—complete musical songs.
It's like handing over a job to a mini band: you hand in a request list or a reference demo, and it combines the vocals and accompaniments and delivers a finished song. The final style of the song depends on the prompts you give; whatever the prompts say, it will be generated accordingly.

fields.精确定义: Synthesize speech to a specific speaker's timbre and style, including cloning timbres from a small number of samples.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
When it comes to voices, AI can "match" or "clone" them: synthesizing the voice of a specific speaker's timbre and style is what AI dubbing and voice cloning are doing. What is synthesized is not just any machine voice, but the voice of a specific speaker; a further step is cloning, which can reproduce the timbre with only a small number of samples.
Two key points: one is "specific", aiming at a specific person's voice and style; the other is "a small number of samples", the threshold is lower than imagined, and a voice can be reproduced with very little material.
It is a serious use for dubbing work to give corresponding voices to designated characters. But we must also keep an eye on it: since sounds can be synthesized and cloned, the old experience of "identifying people by listening to their voices" has to be questioned.

fields.精确定义: A project orchestration method that breaks the task into multiple steps and executes the model cyclically in a preset process (planning-execution-checking).
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
The agent workflow is a project orchestration method: splitting the task into multiple steps and letting the model execute in a cyclical manner in a preset process. Each step follows the rhythm of "planning, execution, and inspection." First think clearly about what to do at this step, do it, and then look at the results after you finish it. If you are not qualified, go back to the process and try again.
There are two key words in it: preset, the process is pre-arranged by people, and the model operates within the framework; cycle, it is not a straight line to the end, but one step at a time, check one step at a time, and then go after checking.
