It's like having a quality inspection station on an assembly line: completed parts are inspected first, if they pass, they go down, if they fail, they are sent back for redoing. Compared with letting AI generate the entire process in one go, this kind of step-by-step choreography makes it easier to detect and correct errors in the process, and the completion of the task is more stable.

fields.精确定义: Multiple agents divide labor, communicate, and collaborate to complete complex tasks, and can cross frameworks and vendors.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
Multi-agent collaboration refers to letting multiple agents do complex tasks together: each takes care of its own tasks, communicates with each other, and works together to get things done. It is a difficult task for an intelligent agent to work alone. It is divided into several parts. Some are for checking information, some are sorting, and some are producing reports. They communicate with each other to align the progress, and then they are put together to complete the task.
Division of labor, communication, and collaboration are its three key words: division of labor is to cut complex tasks into pieces, communication is to exchange information between each company without losing connection, and collaboration is to integrate the output of each company into a whole. This set of coordination can also work across frameworks and manufacturers, and it doesn’t necessarily have to be an agent made by the same company to work together.
It's like a temporary project team: members come from different departments or even different companies, each doing their own specialized work, and relying on communication to bring the results to one place. This is the reason why complex tasks are assigned to "a group" rather than "one".

fields.精确定义: An open protocol that allows AI agents from different frameworks and different vendors to discover each other's capabilities and delegate tasks.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
The Inter-Agent Agreement (A2A) is a set of open protocols that solves the problem of how AI agents built by different frameworks and manufacturers can recognize each other and assign tasks to each other. Two basic actions are stipulated in the agreement: one is to discover each other's abilities and let other agents know "what I can do"; the other is to delegate tasks. Whoever is interested in the ability can officially hand over the work to it.
Just like the rules for doing business between different companies: both parties may not necessarily use the same internal system, but as long as they abide by the same public business agreement, they can hand each other business cards, check what the other party can provide, and then sign a contract for cooperation.
The word "open" is the key: the rules are open to the public, and any smart agent can access it according to them. In this way, agents from different backgrounds can have a common language to work with, instead of each speaking his own words and being isolated from each other.

fields.精确定义: An AI agent that can operate a graphical interface like a human (moving the mouse, clicking, typing, reading screen pixels); among them, a subcategory that specializes in operating web browsers is often called a "browser-using agent".
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.来源依据: Anthropic“Developing a computer use model”；OpenAI“Introducing Operator”
fields.通俗解释:
Computers use intelligent agents, which are AI that can operate graphical interfaces like humans: it can move the mouse, click buttons, type on the keyboard, and can read the pixels on the screen to "see" the current picture. Whatever interface is given on the screen, it will operate according to that interface.
One of these types of agents focuses specifically on web browsers, often called "browser-using agents", which is a subcategory of it.
It's like equipping an AI with a pair of hands that can operate a computer, and a pair of eyes that stare at the screen: it reads whatever is on the screen, and it moves where the cursor should go. What's special about it is that it follows the way ordinary people use computers to click, input, and view. It operates how people operate the interface.

fields.精确定义: AI programmers who can understand the code base, plan independently, modify multi-file code, run tests and submit.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
The AI programming agent can be understood as an AI programmer: it can read the entire code base, plan what to do after receiving the task, move across multiple files together when changing the code, run tests and verify the changes, and finally submit. By putting these few steps together, it can handle the main aspects of writing code.
It is not the same thing as a tool that "just spits out a piece of code": the latter just gives you a piece of ready-made text and it's done, while the former works on the entirety of a real project.
It's like inviting a programmer colleague who can work independently: you don't need to feed you page after page of the project background, it will read it by itself; you don't need to arrange the steps, it will plan by itself; after making the changes, it will run the test and let the results speak for itself. Understand, plan, modify, test, submit, remember this chain, and the concept will stand.

fields.精确定义: The agent breaks the goal into subtasks (planning), and checks, retries, and corrects (reflection) the results of its previous step.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.来源依据: Yao et al. ReAct, arXiv:2210.03629; Shinn et al. Reflexion, arXiv:2303.11366
fields.通俗解释:
For an intelligent agent to accomplish one thing, it relies on two sets of coordinated mechanisms. One is planning: break the big goal into sub-tasks and figure out what to do first and then what to do. The other is reflection: take a look back at the result of the previous step to check whether it was done correctly. If not, try again, correct it, and then move on.
The two are used in tandem: planning governs "how to arrange the route", and reflection governs "whether each step is stable or not." Without planning, tasks are a mess; without reflection, if you make the first mistake, you will end up wrong.
It's like taking an unfamiliar route: dividing the trip into several sections before setting off is planning; checking the map after each section and going back if you find it's off track is reflection. Most of the ability of an intelligent agent lies not in how far it can think in one breath, but in the mechanism of disassembly and review: take a few steps, check one step, and correct mistakes on the spot.

fields.精确定义: A search form in which answers are directly generated from comprehensive search results of large models with sources attached.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
AI search is a new form of conversational search: you ask a question, and the large model combines the retrieved results and directly generates an answer, with the source attached. Unlike the old-fashioned search that gives you a list of links and lets you click on them yourself, it reads them for you first and organizes the key points into a ready-made answer.
There are only two changes in usage: from "give a link" to "give an answer", and from "you turn the web pages one by one" to "it will be explained clearly in one go". The source is given to you along with the answer. There are traces of where the answer comes from.
It's like hiring a reading assistant: In the past, you got a pile of books and had to flip through them yourself; now the assistant will finish flipping through the pages for you, explain them to you, and tell you which books he read them from. The source is attached next to the answer. If you want to delve deeper, you can click to trace it at any time.

fields.精确定义: An AI functional layer embedded in office, programming, design and other software to assist people in completing tasks. The new generation of products is designed around AI capabilities from the first day (called "AI native" applications), rather than hanging an additional AI button on traditional software.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
AI assistant, also called Copilot, refers to the AI functional layer embedded in software such as office, programming, and design: without reinventing the wheel, it helps you complete the task in the software you are working in.
Product form is also divided into two generations: new and old. The old-fashioned approach is to hang an extra AI button on traditional software; the new generation of products is designed around AI capabilities from the first day, and these types of applications are called "AI native" applications. The difference lies in the starting point of the design: one is installed later, and the other is built for AI when the foundation is laid.
The name "co-pilot" is quite appropriate: you are still the main driver of the car, and the co-pilot helps you look at the road, deliver information, and give reminders, and the steering wheel is always in your hands. To judge the role of AI in a product, it depends on whether it is embedded in the work to assist you, or whether it is an extra button hanging on the outside.

fields.精确定义: String text, image, video, and audio generation tools into a complete creative process.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
The AI content creation workflow is to string together text, image, video, and audio generation tools to form a complete creation process. A single tool can only produce one type of finished product. After the process is put together, copywriting, graphics, video, and dubbing can all proceed in succession, and finally merge into a complete work.
For example, let text tools produce copywriting, image tools produce pictures, video tools animate pictures, audio tools add sounds, one link after another, and the output of each link becomes the raw material for the next link.
It's like setting up a small production line: each tool occupies one station, and each one does its own thing. When strung together, it forms a complete link from raw materials to finished products. The key to the chain is the connection. If the previous link matches what the next link requires, the quality of the finished product will stabilize along the process.

fields.精确定义: Requirements are a clear description of the functions that the system should have or the conditions that should be met; users are the people or groups who actually use the product or system. When describing requirements, "use cases/scenarios" are often used: clarify "who will use it to accomplish what under what circumstances."
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the requirements are the technical solutions to be implemented" (the requirements describe the problems to be solved); "the developers themselves are the users".
fields.典型案例: "The library wants students to find books faster" is a demand; "making a search box" is just one of the solutions.
fields.反例: I started making things before I even figured out who was going to use them for what.
fields.深度上限: It only asks "who uses it and what needs to be solved" and does not talk about requirements engineering methods.
fields.安全与伦理边界: When involving real users, their wishes and privacy must be respected and consent must be obtained first.
fields.通俗解释:
Before making something, you must first figure out two things: who will use it and what problem it will solve. Requirements are a clear description of what functions the system should have and what conditions it should achieve; users are the people or groups who actually use this thing. When describing requirements, we often hear expressions such as "use cases" and "scenarios", which are actually clarifying one thing: who, under what circumstances, will use it to accomplish what.
Don't confuse the two. For example, "the library wants students to find books faster" is a need, and "making a search box" is only one of the solutions - think about the needs first, and only then can you choose a solution. Some people think that just because they are developers, they are equal to users. In fact, the developers and users are often not the same group, and their ideas are very different.
The opposite situation is also common: you rush into it before you figure out who is going to use it and what it is used for, and as a result, you end up with something that no one needs. First ask "who uses it and what needs to be solved", and then talk about how to implement it.

fields.精确定义: An early, simplified version used to verify the feasibility of a design idea or feature.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the prototype is the final product" (the prototype is used for exploration and verification, and is usually modified or discarded).
fields.典型案例: Use paper sketches or simple pages to first verify "whether this will work smoothly."
fields.反例: I pursued completeness and precision from the very beginning, but ended up going in the wrong direction and wasting a lot of time.
fields.深度上限: It only does "make a prototype first to verify the idea" and does not talk about prototyping tools and development frameworks.
fields.安全与伦理边界: If prototype testing involves real users, the purpose of the testing must be stated and their information protected.
fields.通俗解释:
Whether the idea is reliable or not, don’t rush to make a complete set, make a sample first and try it out. A prototype is an early simplified version used to verify the feasibility of a design idea or function: a few paper sketches and a simple page. You can try it first to see if it will work smoothly. If the direction is right, then proceed.
Remember its identity: the prototype is for exploration, not the final product. After exploration and verification, it will most likely be modified or even discarded entirely - it doesn't hurt to throw away a sketch, but it would be a big loss to find out half way through that it was in the wrong direction. Some people pursue completeness and refinement right from the start, and all the effort they spent in the previous stage was in vain.
For example, when a tailor makes clothes, he first cuts a sample for you to try on, and then changes the pattern after trying it on. I haven't heard that he doesn't even measure the excess and just sews the finished product directly.

fields.精确定义: The page is the overall interface that users see and operate; components are the reusable functional units that make up the page; status is the data status recorded by the system at the current moment (such as "input" and "loading").
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the interface is just a drawn picture"; ignoring state changes is the real running part of the application.
fields.典型案例: A to-do application: input box (component) → list update (status change) after adding.
fields.反例: We only discuss the beautiful interface, not "what happens after clicking".
fields.深度上限: It only does the identification and relationship sorting of components and states, not the front-end framework and code.
fields.通俗解释:
The interface of an application can be broken down into three things. The page is the overall interface that you see and operate; the components are the reusable functional units that make up the page, such as input boxes and buttons, which can be done in one place and used in multiple places; the status is the data recorded by the system at the current moment, such as "entered" and "loading" are all statuses.
There is something that is easy to overlook: no matter how beautiful the interface is, it is just a shell, and state changes are the real part of the application. Take a to-do application as an example. The input box is a component. If you add a to-do item, the list will be updated accordingly. This update means that the status has changed. If we only discuss whether the interface is beautiful or not and do not discuss "what will happen after clicking", it is equivalent to only looking at the photos and not seeing how the machine operates.
Think of pages as rooms, components as furniture, and states as light switches, and the relationship between the three will become clear.

fields.精确定义: User evaluation information on product experience and effects is the basis for improvement.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the more feedback, the better" (it is necessary to distinguish between representativeness, noise and real needs); "whatever users say will be changed."
fields.典型案例: The tester said "the button cannot be found", adjusted the position accordingly and tested again.
fields.反例: Feedback is collected but never modified based on it.
fields.深度上限: It only does "collection-classification-judgment of which ones are worth changing" and does not talk about user research methods.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Collecting feedback requires consent and protects participant information.
fields.通俗解释:
Whether something is done well or not, the users have the most say. User feedback is the user's evaluation information on the product experience and effect, which is the basis for improvement. For example, if the trial user says "the button cannot be found," you adjust the button position accordingly and let the user try it again - this is how the feedback becomes modified.
But don’t just accept all the feedback. The more the better. The feedback is mixed with representative opinions, noise and superficial requirements, which must be classified and judged as to which ones are real needs and which ones are worth changing. Just change whatever the user says, and the more you change, the more messy it becomes; collecting a lot but never modifying it based on it is equally useless - the value of feedback lies in "use", not in "storage".
There’s also a bottom line: feedback must be collected with consent, and participants’ information cannot be leaked.

fields.精确定义: A description of how data is passed, transformed, and stored between parts of the system.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "data flow is network traffic"; ignoring where the data is processed and saved.
fields.典型案例: The flow of "user input → save to form → read and calculate → display results".
fields.反例: It is unclear where the data comes from, where it is stored, and who can see it.
fields.深度上限: It only does flow sorting and annotation of personal information, and does not talk about data architecture.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Wherever personal information is involved in the data stream, it must be marked and how it is protected.
fields.通俗解释:
There are routes for how data travels in a system. Data flow refers to how data is transferred, converted and stored between various parts of the system: where it comes from, how it is processed on the way, and where it is finally stored. For example, "user input → save to table → read and calculate → display the result", this is a clear flow.
There is a misunderstanding to clarify: data flow is not equal to network traffic. Traffic is only about how much data is running on the pipeline. Data flow is concerned with the step at which the data is processed and saved. If it is unclear "where the data comes from, where it is stored, and who can see it," the accounting system will be confused.
There is another step that cannot be omitted when sorting out the flow: all locations involving personal information must be marked and how to protect them must be explained.

fields.精确定义: The interface is a channel for exchanging data and calling functions between software systems according to agreed rules; model calling is the process in which the application delivers user input and data to the model through the interface and then retrieves the results.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the interface is a button for ordinary users to click" (the interface is for program calls).
fields.典型案例: The application sends questions to the model through the interface, and then displays the answers.
fields.反例: It is thought that the application itself has the entire large model "built-in".
fields.深度上限: It only explains "exchanging input and output according to the agreement" and does not translate into API programming, key management and authentication.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Keys and permissions may not be published or written into student work.
fields.来源依据: Master §3.4 Depth Upper Limit; Unified Boundary "The interface only explains that the system exchanges input and output according to the agreement"
fields.通俗解释:
Many AI applications don't "think" on their own, they ask models for help. What helps it connect is called an interface - a channel through which software systems exchange data and call functions according to agreed rules. Model call is a specific transaction: the application passes user input and data to the model through the interface, and then retrieves the results and displays them.
Note that the interface is not a button for people to click. It is oriented to program calls. The program delivers things and receives results according to the agreed format. Don't think that the application itself has the entire large model "built-in" - most of the time, the model runs remotely, and the application is only responsible for sending questions and getting answers back. It's like the laboratory test window in a hospital: Send in the sample, get the report as agreed, and don't worry about how the test was done in the middle.
Remembering the division of labor in this channel, many questions of "how do applications use AI" will be solved.

fields.精确定义: An iterative process of improving the product through multiple rounds based on feedback.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "iteration means repeated redoing" (each round should make directional improvements based on evidence and goals).
fields.典型案例: The first version can be run → found missing boundary conditions → modified → retest.
fields.反例: Every time I change it, I just change it based on my feelings, without any basis.
fields.深度上限: It only does "change it once based on the evidence and retest it", and does not talk about version management and release pipelines.
fields.安全与伦理边界: A record of modifications should be kept, explaining what was changed and why.
fields.通俗解释:
Good things are rarely done right the first time, but are mostly made through repeated revisions. Based on feedback, multiple rounds of improvements are made to the product. This repetitive process is called iteration: the first version works, but it is found that boundary conditions are missed, revised, tested again, and then goes around again.
Iteration does not mean redoing over and over again. Each round should have a direction: revise based on the evidence and goals, verify the revisions, and confirm what has been improved before moving on to the next round. If you change the pattern every time based on your feelings, and you can’t say what’s good or why you changed it, that’s not iteration, it’s just messing around.
It's like revising an essay: after receiving the comments, you change the beginning of this draft and add examples in the next draft. Each draft is closer to what you want than the last draft - instead of starting over and writing another one based on your mood.

fields.精确定义: Specific inputs, operational steps, and expected results specified to verify that the system meets requirements.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "the test case is just a casual try" (it needs to have clear input and expectations and can be executed repeatedly).
fields.典型案例: Design three types of use cases for the login function: "normal password", "wrong password" and "empty password".
fields.反例: Only test the path that you know will lead to success.
fields.深度上限: It only designs three types of use cases: normal, boundary, and abnormal, and does not talk about automated test engineering.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Failures and exceptions must be recorded truthfully, and only successes must not be reported.
fields.通俗解释:
How to prove that a function is really reliable? Make a list of situations to try out in advance. Test cases are specific inputs, operation steps and expected results specified to check whether the system meets the requirements - what to give, how to operate, and what should be produced. If the three items are written clearly, anyone who does it can get the accuracy and can be executed repeatedly.
Just give it a try with a few clicks, that doesn’t count as a test design. For example, arranging use cases for the login function: normal passwords should be able to enter, incorrect passwords should be blocked, and empty passwords should have prompts - normal, boundary, and abnormal categories are all covered, and the function can be considered thoroughly tested. Only testing the path that you know will lead to success is tantamount to avoiding the most important and taking the easy way out.
Failures and exceptions in the test must be recorded truthfully, and you cannot only report the half that is successful.

fields.精确定义: The process of locating the causes of failure phenomena during testing, selecting modification objects, retesting after modification, and explaining the results.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "failure means something was done badly" (failure is necessary information for improvement); "just change it until it is usable, there is no need to explain the reasons".
fields.典型案例: It is found that the output is garbled. It is determined that the input is not checked. After the check is made, the retest passes.
fields.反例: Try again and again until you accidentally succeed without knowing why.
fields.深度上限: It only records "positioning-modification-retesting" and does not talk about debugging tools and performance tuning.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Records of failures must be kept; "ultimate success" must not be used to cover up problems in the process.
fields.来源依据: Master Version §2.2 Judgment Optimization "Failure Recording, Modification and Retesting"
fields.通俗解释:
If something goes wrong in the test, don't get upset right now - the question itself carries information. Failure analysis and repair is a complete process: locate the cause of the failure, select the object to be modified, complete the modification and retest, and then explain the results clearly. It was found that the output was garbled, and it was found that the input was not checked. After the check was made and the retest passed, it was repaired.
Some people regard failure as "bad work", but in fact failure is necessary information for improvement; some people just make it work and call it a day, without explaining the reasons, and they will fail again next time. The most important thing to guard against is to try again and again until you accidentally succeed, but don't know why it worked - the problem is still buried underneath, but it hasn't exploded yet.
It's like checking for water leaks at home: find the cracked area, fix it, and then run the water to check again; instead of holding a basin under it and waiting until it stops dripping, then it's done.

fields.精确定义: The overall relationship between how the various parts of the application (interface, data, processing logic, models and external services) are combined and collaborated.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "an application is just a page"; ignoring the cooperation of behind-the-scenes data, processing and external services.
fields.典型案例: Draw the structural relationship diagram of "interface-data-model-output".
fields.反例: Just draw a screenshot of the interface as the system structure.
fields.深度上限: We only sort out the structural relationships and do not talk about the production-level system architecture.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The parts of the structure that involve data and permissions must indicate where responsibilities lie.
fields.来源依据: Master §3.4 "Page, component, data, state, model call, workflow"
fields.通俗解释:
When you click on an app, all you see is the interface, and there is a whole lot of coordination behind it. The application structure refers to the overall relationship between how the interface, data, processing logic, model and external services are combined and how they collaborate. Draw a structural relationship diagram of "interface-data-model-output". You can see clearly at a glance who is connected to whom and where the data is going.
The most common mistake is to treat the application as "a page" and only use screenshots of the interface as the system structure. But behind the interface, data is being accessed, logic is being calculated, models are producing results, and external services are responding. If any link is missing, the page in front of you will be dead.
It's like looking at a restaurant: the front hall is the interface, the warehouse is the data, the back kitchen is the processing logic, and the delivery platform is the external service - no matter how beautiful the front hall is, if the back kitchen cannot operate, the guests will still not be able to eat.

fields.精确定义: Deployment is the process of releasing the system to a running environment that can be used by users; release judgment is the decision whether to make it public after checking the facts, privacy, security, copyright and platform rules.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "deployment means writing the code"; "it should be released as soon as it is done".
fields.典型案例: Before publishing, check whether it contains other people's photos, whether it is marked as generated by AI, and whether it complies with platform rules.
fields.反例: Send unfinished works directly to the public platform.
fields.深度上限: The focus is on release conditions, security checks and judgment on whether to release, not on operation and maintenance.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Whether to publish must be decided by those who comply with the rules. The course does not set public release as a unified condition for meeting standards.
fields.来源依据: Master §3.4 Unified Boundaries; §8.3 Public Release Security
fields.通俗解释:
Just because the work is finished doesn’t mean it should be sent out. Deployment is the process of putting the system into a running environment that can be used by users; release judgment is the decision whether to make it public after checking the facts, privacy, security, copyright and platform rules. These are two hurdles that cannot be skipped in one step by "writing the code".
What should I check before posting? For example, whether there are other people's photos in the work, whether it is marked as generated by AI, and whether it complies with the platform's rules - check it out and then decide whether to post it or not, and how to post it. Post the work that has not been inspected directly to the public platform. If there is a problem, it cannot be taken back.
There is one more thing to say up front: whether to publish or not must be decided by those who comply with the rules. Just because something is made does not mean it must be made public. Whether to send or not is a question of judgment, not a default action.

fields.精确定义: Organize goals, context, materials, constraints, steps, and output requirements into task statements that a person or system can perform and check.
fields.常见误解: Misunderstood as "the longer and more detailed the better"; ignoring "checkable standards".
fields.典型案例: Write "make a class photo album" into a task statement including objects, materials, steps, finished product requirements and inspection standards.
fields.反例: Just give a vague request and let others (or AI) do it.
fields.深度上限: It only does "clearly stated + checkable" and does not follow professional document standards.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Mission statements must not contain unauthorized information about others.
fields.来源依据: Master §2.2 Expression Design; §6.4 Prompt Word Scaffolding Field
fields.通俗解释:
Before handing over the work, think about whether the other party can follow it and whether it can be accepted after it is completed. A mission statement is a description that organizes goals, background, materials, constraints, steps, and output requirements so that a person or system can execute and check it.
Don't think that the longer and more detailed the description is, the better. The key is "checkability": saying "make a class photo album" is not as good as writing a complete task description - who will use it, what materials are on hand, how many steps it will be done, what the finished product will look like, and what standards will be used to qualify it. The inspection standard is the easiest to miss, but without it, everyone can only talk about their own things after everything is done.
Just give a vague request and let people (or AI) take action, and you will probably get a result you don't want. It's like opening a demand order to the decoration team: the style, materials, construction period, and acceptance criteria are all written down, so it's not easy to argue.

fields.精确定义: Organize effective practices into method assets that can be used next time: record task conditions, necessary inputs, valid steps, variable content, output requirements and inspection methods, and verify whether they can be reused through new tasks.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "saving a fixed instruction is enough to settle"; "the method can be copied regardless of the conditions".
fields.典型案例: Write the "Steps + Checklist for Organizing Information" into a task guide, and use it again with a new topic.
fields.反例: The last time it worked, it was directly applied to a completely different task.
fields.深度上限: It starts with task guides and replaceable templates and develops into work modules and skills without being tied to a single platform.
fields.安全与伦理边界: If the method contains other people's information or authorized materials, authorization must be re-confirmed before reuse.
fields.通俗解释:
Once one thing is done, don't let the experience be lost along with the mission. Method precipitation is to organize effective practices into method assets that can be used next time: record task conditions, necessary inputs, effective steps, what content can be replaced, what are the output requirements, how to check, and then try it with a new task to verify that it can really be reused.
Saving only a fixed instruction does not count as precipitation - the instruction is dead and will fail as soon as the conditions change. Methods cannot be copied without asking for conditions. The routine that worked last time will probably go wrong when applied to a completely different task. For example, organize problem-solving ideas into notes: clearly note which question types are applicable and what conditions are missing so that they cannot be used. Next time, focus on the question types first before writing.
You can start with task guides and replaceable templates, and gradually grow them into work modules that can be used over and over again. If the method contains other people's information or authorized materials, authorization must be re-confirmed before reuse.

fields.精确定义: Determine whether a result truly solves a meaningful problem: explain who it serves, what value it brings, what new ideas it has, and what impact it may have.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "having new functions means innovation"; "advanced technology means having value".
fields.典型案例: Compare a "cool but no one uses" idea with a "modest but really useful" solution.
fields.反例: It only pursues dazzling effects without solving problems.
fields.深度上限: We only make judgments about "who we serve, what use it is, and what impact it has," without talking about the business model.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Value judgments should also consider use, safety, rights and social impact.
fields.通俗解释:
When evaluating a result, don’t first ask whether it’s cool or not, first ask whose problem it solves. Innovation value judgment is to judge whether the result really solves a meaningful problem, and clearly states four things: who it serves, what value it brings, what new ideas it has, and what impact it may have.
Having new functions does not mean innovation, and technological advancement does not mean having value. Comparing a "cool but no one uses" idea with a "simple but really useful" solution, the answer comes out: if there are no real problems behind the cool effects, the fun will be over.
When making this judgment, you must also spread the word: use, safety, rights, and social impact are all taken into consideration. Whether a tool is good or not depends on how well it fits your hand, and does not depend on how fancy the pattern on the handle is.

5-15.name: API (Application Programming Interface) and API Key (Safety Perspective)

fields.精确定义: API is the channel for "allowing programs to call AI capabilities"; API Key is the "pass/ID card" to be used when calling. It is essentially a string of permission credentials. Once leaked, others can use your credit or even access your data.
fields.常见误解: Treat the API Key as an "inconsequential string of characters" and post it to a public webpage or share it with others.
fields.典型案例: Explain "why it is dangerous to send the key to the public group" and how to deal with it after it is leaked (immediately invalidate and regenerate).
fields.反例: Think of Key as "setting a password at will" or "hard-coding it in the code and sharing it".
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the security common sense of "this is a credential, it cannot be leaked, and it will be invalid if it is leaked", but not how to write the calling code.
fields.安全与伦理边界: (This card is limited to a safety education perspective and does not involve programming.)
fields.教学类比: Like home keys: You don’t need to be able to match keys, but you must never take photos of keys and post them online.
fields.通俗解释:
To use AI capabilities, a program relies on two things: a channel and a pass. The channel is called API, which is the interface that allows the program to call AI capabilities; the pass is called API Key, which is the certificate that needs to be presented when calling. In the final analysis, it is a string of permission certificates - it recognizes "you are qualified to use it."
The important thing is here: once the Key is leaked, others can use your credit and even access your data. Treating it as an "inconsequential string of characters" and casually posting it on a public webpage or sending it to a group chat is equivalent to taking a photo of your home key and posting it online - you don't need to know how to match the key, but you must never let the key fall into the hands of outsiders.
What if it's leaked? Immediately invalidate and regenerate. Keep this in mind.

fields.精确定义: A place that concentrates a large number of AI chips to provide computing power for training and running large models can be understood as a "factory for producing AI capabilities." Every time you ask AI to answer, it is consuming power and machines behind the scenes.
fields.常见误解: Think of the intelligent computing center as "a supercomputer"; or think that "AI does not consume resources."
fields.典型案例: Understand "why training a large model requires tens of thousands of chips to be worked on for several months at the same time." (Co-referenced with 5-21 "Computing Power": This card talks about "where the place is", 5-21 talks about "how fast the work is done")
fields.反例: Thinking that "AI is virtual and does not consume resources."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the role of "a place that centrally provides computing power" and does not talk about the computer room architecture and hardware technology.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The concentration of computing power brings about energy consumption and environmental impact, leading to K6.
fields.教学类比: Like a power plant: you use the lights at home, but the electricity is concentrated from a power plant far away.
fields.来源依据: Master version §3.1 K5 + industry common saying
fields.通俗解释:
Every time you ask AI a question, there is a factory in the distance turning on the machine for you. Supercomputing centers and intelligent computing centers are places where a large number of AI chips are concentrated to provide computing power for training and running large models. They can be understood as "factories for producing AI capabilities" - training large models requires tens of thousands of chips to be operated at the same time for several months. This kind of work can only be done in such centralized venues.
Don’t think of it as “a supercomputer,” which is a big place where thousands of chips come together to work; and don’t think of AI as virtual and not consuming resources—every time you ask AI to answer, it is consuming power and machines behind the scenes.
Just like the lights at home: you are the one using the electricity, and the power is generated by a distant power plant. The same goes for AI capabilities. You are used and the intelligent computing center contributes.

fields.精确定义: AI services are often charged based on the "number of tokens used", just like taxi rides are charged based on mileage. The cost of inference refers to the amount of money it costs each time to let the AI ​​work (computing power, electricity bills, machine depreciation, etc.). These two concepts determine whether AI is "expensive" to use.
fields.常见误解: Thinks "AI usage is free and unlimited"; doesn't understand why long answers are more expensive than short answers.
fields.典型案例: Compare the cost difference between short answers and long-form output, and understand that “making AI talk less nonsense can also save money.”
fields.反例: Think of "free quota" as "always free."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the intuition of "pay according to usage, and the cost varies", and does not talk about pricing strategies and business details.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Cost awareness helps students form a resource concept of "reasonable use and no waste".
fields.教学类比: It's like using the meter when taking a taxi: the farther the journey is and the longer the time, the more the meter will jump.
fields.通俗解释:
Using AI costs money, and how you calculate the accounts is important. AI services are often charged based on the "number of words used"; the inference cost refers to the money spent each time the AI ​​works - computing power, electricity costs, and machine depreciation are all included in it. The combination of these two concepts determines whether AI is expensive to use.
For example, it's like using the meter when taking a taxi: the farther the journey is and the longer the time, the more the meter will jump. The same goes for AI. The more words it uses, the higher the bill will be - this is why long answers are more expensive than short answers, and why "making AI talk less nonsense" can actually save money.
There are two misunderstandings to avoid: First, you think that AI use is free and unlimited. In fact, many services only provide free quotas, and you will still be billed if you exceed the limit; second, you do not realize that there is a real cost of money behind every conversation. Only when you have this account in your mind can you use it appropriately.

fields.精确定义: Putting AI on a remote server for everyone to use is called cloud deployment (more powerful, pay-as-you-go, but the data must be uploaded to the cloud); installing the model to run locally on your own device is called local deployment (good privacy, available offline, but capabilities are limited by the device). Both have their own trade-offs. In order to fit the model into devices such as mobile phones, it will technically be compressed and made smaller (this is called quantization), which may cause a slight loss of accuracy.
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "the local environment must be worse" or "the cloud must be unsafe"; ignoring the scenario determines the choice.
fields.典型案例: Discussing "When processing private class photos, should we use cloud or local tools?" New mobile phones can translate and retouch images offline, relying on small models that are quantized and compressed and then installed locally.
fields.反例: All data is uploaded to the cloud indiscriminately; it is thought that "the AI running on the mobile phone and the cloud are the same model."
fields.深度上限: We only talk about the choices and applicable scenarios of the two forms, not the deployment technology.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Prioritizing localization/desensitization in privacy-sensitive scenarios is an important security judgment.
fields.教学类比: Like cooking at home vs. ordering takeout: one is privacy controllable but troublesome, the other is convenient but requires telling others about your needs.
fields.通俗解释:
The same AI can live in a remote computer room or be installed on your mobile phone. Putting it on a remote server for everyone to use is called cloud deployment: it has stronger capabilities and pays on demand, but the data needs to be uploaded. Installing it and running it locally on your own device is called local deployment: it has good privacy and can be used offline, but its capabilities may be limited by the device. Both paths have trade-offs, which one you choose depends on the scene.
In order to fit the model into a device such as a mobile phone, it is technically compressed and made smaller. This is called quantization, and the cost may be a slight loss of accuracy. New mobile phones can translate and retouch images offline, relying on a small model that is compressed and installed locally - it is not the same as the large model in the cloud.
Don’t conclude that “on-premises must be worse” or “the cloud must be unsafe”. Like cooking at home and ordering takeout: one has controllable privacy but is troublesome, the other saves trouble but needs to be communicated to others. When dealing with things like private class photos, you should think carefully before choosing.

fields.精确定义: It refers to someone using carefully designed input to trick the AI into revealing information it shouldn't say, breaking the rules it should abide by, or performing actions it shouldn't. Direct input to the AI ​​is called "prompt injection", inducing it to bypass security restrictions is called "jailbreaking" or "sandbox escape"; if instructions are secretly buried through external content such as web pages and documents, it is called "indirect prompt injection".
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "as long as the model is strong enough, it will not be fooled"; ignoring that such attacks exploit the normal working mode of the model rather than program vulnerabilities.
fields.典型案例: Discuss "Why does AI follow a sentence hidden in a web page" and understand the real risks of indirect injection.
fields.反例: Think of "AI has security limitations" as "AI must not be bypassed."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "what this type of attack is and why it is so difficult to prevent", but does not talk about the technical details of attack and protection. AI systems also have more covert attack methods such as data poisoning and adversarial samples, which are studied by professional security personnel and will not be covered in this course.
fields.安全与伦理边界: This card is about technical safety education; see K6 for social impact and responsibility.
fields.教学类比: Just say to the doorman "I am sent by the boss" and he will let you go - the trick is to deceive the judge, not to smash the door.
fields.来源依据: OWASP LLM Top 10 (Prompt Injection is listed as LLM01)
fields.通俗解释:
When the AI is tricked, there is often no need to pick the lock and break down the door - it works as usual, but is fed bad words. Using carefully designed input to induce the AI ​​to leak information it shouldn't say, break the rules it should abide by, and perform operations it shouldn't perform, this type of attack is called prompt injection; specifically inducing it to bypass security restrictions is called jailbreaking or sandbox escape; if the instructions are secretly buried in web pages or documents, and the AI ​​reads it and follows it, that's called indirect prompt injection.
Some people think that "if the model is strong enough, it will not be deceived." This is wrong. This type of attack does not exploit program vulnerabilities, but the normal working mode of the model - it is born to read input and follow instructions, which is why it is hard to prevent.
Just like saying to the doorman "I am sent by the boss", the doorman will let you go. The trick is to judge, not to smash the door, so no matter how strong the door is, it is not safe.

fields.精确定义: Refers to a chip specially used to run AI calculations. The graphics card (GPU), which was originally used for rendering game screens, was later found to be particularly good at AI and became the "engine" of AI. There is also a small chip specially designed for AI called NPU, which is installed in mobile phones and allows mobile phones to recognize, edit and translate images without being connected to the Internet.
fields.常见误解: Treat the chip as "software"; or think that "AI does not require specialized hardware."
fields.典型案例: Look at the "built-in NPU" promoted by mobile phones to understand why mobile phones can translate offline and automatically beautify photos. In the past two years, countries have been competing to build local AI chips and computing power clusters - chips have become strategic resources.
fields.反例: I thought "any computer can run large models."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the intuition that "there are specialized hardware and different chips have their own strengths", and does not talk about the number of cores, frequencies, and architectural parameters.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Chips are high-end manufacturing and are related to industry and geopolitical issues, which can lead to K6.
fields.教学类比: Like different tools: a hammer for hammering nails, a screwdriver for screwing screws - AI also has its most handy "tool chip".
fields.通俗解释:
Where does the power of AI come from? from a specialized class of chips. The graphics card (GPU), which was originally used for rendering game screens, was later found to be particularly good at AI, and became the "engine" of AI. There is also a small chip NPU designed specifically for AI, which is installed in mobile phones, allowing mobile phones to recognize, edit, and translate images without being connected to the Internet. When I see a mobile phone advertising “built-in NPU”, that’s it.
Two misunderstandings need to be clarified: a chip is not software, it is a piece of real hardware; AI does not require specialized hardware - the phrase "any computer can run large models" is probably unreliable. Different chips have their own strengths. Just like a hammer hammers nails and a screwdriver twists screws, AI also has its favorite tool.
Chips are still high-end manufacturing. In the past two years, countries have been competing to build their own AI chips and computing power clusters, and it has become a strategic resource.

fields.精确定义: Refers to the "speed and total amount of work" of the computing device, which is the basic resource for training and running AI. The greater the computing power, the stronger and faster the model that can be run, but it also requires more chips and more electricity. The term "computing power anxiety" refers to the worry about insufficient computing power.
fields.常见误解: Confusing "computing power" with "algorithm" or "data"; thinking that "computing power is unlimited".
fields.典型案例: Understand "why it takes tens of thousands of chips to train a large model and it takes a long time" - if the computing power is not enough, it will be slow and expensive. (Reciprocal reference with 5-16 "Supercomputing Center": this card talks about "fast or not", 5-16 talks about "where to calculate".)
fields.反例: It is believed that "AI is virtual and does not consume physical resources."
fields.深度上限: We only talk about the intuition of "computing power = speed and scale of work", and do not talk about units and conversions such as FLOPS/EFLOPS.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Concentration of computing power brings pressure on energy consumption and environment, leading to K6.
fields.教学类比: Like manpower: 10 people can do the same thing at a completely different speed than 1,000 people, but 1,000 people also have to eat more.
fields.通俗解释:
There is a word in the AI world called computing power, which refers to the speed and total amount of work done by computing equipment. It is the basic resource for training and running AI: the greater the computing power, the stronger and faster the model that can be run, but correspondingly, more chips and more power are required. Why does it take a long time to train a large model with tens of thousands of chips? Just because it has a large computing power, if the computing power is insufficient, it will be slow and expensive.
People often confuse computing power with algorithms and data. These three are not the same thing. Don’t think that computing power is unlimited. It is actually connected to machines and electricity. The term "computing power anxiety" refers to the worry about insufficient computing power.
Like manpower work: the same thing, 10 people do it and 1,000 people do it, the speed is completely different, but 1,000 people also need to eat more food-the greater the strength, the greater the appetite.

fields.精确定义: Data centers are buildings filled with servers, where the “brains” of AI live and work 24 hours a day. So many machines heat up very hot together. Traditionally, they were blown by wind (air cooling). Now many of them are directly soaked in special liquid to cool down (liquid cooling), which is fast and saves electricity.
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "AI exists in the cloud and has no entity"; ignoring the huge consumption of electricity and water in data centers.
fields.典型案例: Watch news or videos about "immersion liquid cooling" to understand why servers need to "take a bath."
fields.反例: It is thought that "the data center consumes no power and does not generate heat."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the intuition of "there is a physical place and needs to dissipate and cool down", and does not talk about technical indicators such as PUE and power density.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Data center energy consumption and environmental impact are the basis for understanding the discussion of "whether AI is environmentally friendly". According to estimates by the International Energy Agency (IEA), global data centers will consume approximately 415 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity in 2024, accounting for approximately 1.5% of global electricity consumption, and are expected to double in 2030.
fields.教学类比: For example, in the summer, computers will get hot if they are turned on for a long time - tens of thousands of them in the data center will get hot at the same time, so special methods must be used to cool them down.
fields.通俗解释:
Clouds cannot be seen or touched, but the building containing the clouds is real. A data center is a building filled with servers, where the "brain" of AI lives and works 24 hours a day. So many machines are crowded together and generate heat, which is very hot - think about your computer being hot if you turn it on for a long time. In a data center, tens of thousands of machines are hot at the same time. Cooling down is a big deal.
The old method is to use wind to blow, which is called air cooling; now many buildings directly soak the servers in special liquid to cool down, which is called liquid cooling, which cools down quickly and saves electricity. Herein lies the misunderstanding: I think that if AI exists in the "cloud", it has no physical entity and consumes nothing. In fact, data centers consume a lot of electricity and water. This is an unavoidable issue when discussing whether "AI is environmentally friendly".
Next time you see the news about the server taking a bath, you will understand what is going on.

fields.精确定义: It refers to using AI to help humans do scientific research - such as predicting protein structures, finding new materials, and predicting the weather. It turns AI from a "chat tool" into a "scientific research assistant." The 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry will be awarded to the researchers of AlphaFold, marking that this path has received the highest recognition in the scientific community.
fields.常见误解: Thinking that "AI for Science means AI writing papers"; ignoring that what it really does is "prediction and calculation", scientific judgment still relies on humans.
fields.典型案例: Understand that AI can already help scientists predict weather, find new drugs, and design materials, and discuss "what AI can and cannot do for science."
fields.反例: Thinking that "AI can replace scientists in making discoveries."
fields.深度上限: It only talks about the value and boundary of "AI is a scientific research assistant" and does not talk about the details of models in specific scientific fields.
fields.安全与伦理边界: The attribution and open source sharing of AI-assisted discovery results are issues worthy of discussion.
fields.教学类比: It's like giving a scientist a "fast calculation assistant" - it speeds up calculations, but it's still the scientist's job to ask good questions and judge the results.
fields.通俗解释:
AI can not only chat, but also help scientists do research. Using AI to assist scientific research is called AI for Science: predicting protein structure, finding new materials, and predicting the weather are all tasks it is already doing. The 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry will be awarded to the researchers of AlphaFold. This path has received the highest recognition from the scientific community.
Its role is that of a scientific research assistant: turning AI from a chat tool into a tool that helps science work, accelerating prediction and calculation. But scientific judgment still relies on humans—asking good questions, understanding results, and drawing conclusions are the job of scientists, and AI cannot do it. Therefore, "AI can replace scientists in making discoveries" is a misunderstanding, and "AI for Science means AI writing papers" is also a misunderstanding. Its real focus is on prediction and calculation.
It's like giving a scientist an assistant who can calculate quickly: it calculates the numbers and asks the questions.

fields.精确定义: A platform for designing, running, and monitoring multi-step agent processes, including conditional branches, loops, and retries.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
An intelligent agent process often has more than one step: what to do first, what to do next, how to judge in the middle, and what to do if something goes wrong, all have to be arranged by someone. The automation orchestration platform is a platform used to design, run, and monitor multi-step agent processes.
It takes care of three troubles. Conditional branching: which way to go if certain conditions are met, like the traffic light at an intersection that determines where the car should turn; looping: a certain process needs to be executed repeatedly to let it go around in a circle; retry: if a certain step fails, it will be repeated automatically, without anyone having to watch and click the mouse. With these, the process can turn around on its own, and people can watch it run on the platform.
It's like traffic dispatch: traffic light tubes are diverted, roundabouts are circled, and if there is a traffic jam, re-plan the route before walking - every step is planned.

fields.精确定义: Build applications and workflows based on large models through visual configuration instead of programming.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
You can build an AI application without writing code. No-code, low-code, is this way: through visual configuration, rather than programming, to build applications and workflows based on large models. Some do not use code in the entire process, and some only leave a little handwriting. The threshold is lowered again and again.
This type of platform makes commonly used capabilities into ready-made components: connect models, set up processes, and define input and output. You can just string them together according to your own needs, without having to start with making parts.
It's like building blocks: the bricks are ready-made, but what you have to think about is how to build them. The threshold has been lowered. Whether you can build something useful depends on whether you think clearly about the task itself.

fields.精确定义: Risk list, authority boundaries, responsibility attribution and audit requirements for autonomous agents.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.通俗解释:
If an intelligent agent can work on its own, someone must set rules for it. Agent governance and responsibility refers to a set of management requirements surrounding autonomous agents: risk list, authority boundaries, responsibility attribution, and audit requirements. Each of the four things has its own use.
The risk list is to list in advance what things may go wrong; the authority boundary is to clearly define what it can touch and what it cannot touch, so as not to let it have too much power to do things; the responsibility attribution is to say in advance who will be responsible for problems, and no blame can be given when something goes wrong; the audit requirement is to have records of what it has done and can check it. The more autonomous the agent becomes, the less necessary it is to do these four things.
For example, a company arranges for new employees to take up their posts: a work badge is issued to limit the rooms they can enter, the job description clearly states the responsibilities, handover documents are provided, and work records are left for future reference. Only when the rules are up front do you dare to let it go.

fields.精确定义: The practical application of AI in medical care (auxiliary diagnosis, drug research and development), education (personalized learning, intelligent learning companions), manufacturing (quality inspection, robots) and other industries.
fields.深度上限: Cognitive level to be determined (evolution layer merged)
fields.来源依据: Ministry of Education "Guidelines for the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Primary and Secondary Schools (2025 Edition)"
fields.通俗解释:
AI has long since left the chat box and entered hospitals, schools and factories. In medicine, it helps with auxiliary diagnosis and participates in drug research and development; in education, it supports personalized learning and serves as an intelligent learning companion for students; in manufacturing, it does quality inspection and drives robots. The same AI technology enters different industries and takes on different jobs.
The four words "auxiliary diagnosis" are worth licking: auxiliary means helping the doctor to see, but the doctor still has the decision. What AI does in these industries is the tasks it is good at, and people keep their positions.
Think of it like electricity and you will understand: electricity is not something that can only do one kind of work. Whichever industry it enters, it will be connected to the machines in which industry and can perform different tasks.

fields.精确定义: Misleading information refers to inaccurate information, which is deliberately created and spread to deceive people who call it false information; both are more likely to spread in the AI era due to the lowering of the threshold for generation. In English, Misinformation is often translated as "wrong information/misinformation" (excluding intentionality), and Disinformation is translated as "false information" (deliberate deception) - the key to the distinction is "whether it is intentional or not."
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "AI-generated content is credible if it looks smooth" (fluency is not necessarily related to authenticity).
fields.典型案例: "News screenshots" synthesized by AI are forwarded in the group.
fields.反例: Because "the picture has a source watermark", it is deemed to be genuine.
fields.深度上限: We only make judgments by "looking at the source, finding the original source, and comparing multiple sources" without talking about communication theory.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Do not create or disseminate unverified information; verify before forwarding.
fields.通俗解释:
The same piece of fake news, accidentally transferred to the wrong news, and deliberately made up to deceive people, are completely different in nature. "Misleading information" refers to inaccurate information; among them, information that is deliberately created and used specifically to deceive people is also called "false information." The difference between the two is like saying something wrong unintentionally and lying deliberately. The key lies in whether there is intentional deception. In the AI ​​​​era, the threshold for creating fake content has been greatly lowered. The "news screenshots" synthesized by AI are circulated in the group, and they look like noses and eyes, and they spread much faster than before.
In English, these two words are also divided: Misinformation is often translated as "wrong information", which does not contain intentionality; Disinformation is translated as "false information", which means deliberate deception.
There is one thing that is easy to confuse: just because the content generated by AI reads smoothly and fluently, does not mean it is credible - there is no necessary relationship between smoothness and authenticity. There are three ways to judge: see who the source is, find the original source, and find several more sources to compare. If there is a source watermark on the picture, you don’t have to believe it. It will only count after verification.

fields.精确定义: Algorithmic bias refers to the systematic unfair results of algorithms or models against specific groups due to data, design or usage; fairness refers to the nature of AI systems that do not produce unreasonable differential treatment between different groups.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "algorithms are mathematics and are naturally objective and unbiased"; "there is a single standard answer to fairness" (different definitions of fairness may conflict with each other).
fields.典型案例: Recruitment screening tools give unfair results because historical data favors certain types of people.
fields.反例: Excuse responsibility for the results on the grounds that they were "calculated by a machine".
fields.深度上限: It only makes judgments about "whether there is unfairness, why, and how to reduce it", and does not talk about formal statistical fairness indicators.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Fairness issues involve the rights and interests of real people and must be taken seriously and how to deal with them must be explained.
fields.来源依据: NIST AI RMF (AI bias classification); Master §6.3
fields.通俗解释:
Algorithms are mathematics, so they should be naturally objective? uncertain. Algorithmic bias refers to when an algorithm or model gives systematically unfair results to specific groups due to problems with data, design, or usage. The most typical one is the recruitment screening tool - historical data is inherently biased towards certain types of people, and after the model is learned, it will still produce unfair results. Just like learning a craft from an eccentric master, the craftsmanship learned by the apprentice will also be biased, and the machine will not automatically correct this bias.
"Fairness" means that the AI ​​system does not engage in unreasonable differential treatment between different groups. It should be noted that there is no single standard answer to fairness, and several definitions of fairness may even conflict with each other.
Taking "the machine calculated it" as a sign of immunity is the best idea to avoid: if the result is unfair, it is still unfair. When encountering this kind of thing, there are three things to ask: Is it unfair? Why? How to reduce it?

fields.精确定义: Explainability refers to the nature of the operating mechanism and output basis of an AI system that can be understood and explained by humans; explainable AI (XAI) is its corresponding research direction.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "interpretability equals certain accuracy" (explainability does not guarantee correctness, and vice versa).
fields.典型案例: The tool is required to explain “what information the judgment is based on”.
fields.反例: The result cannot be explained, but it requires others to believe it.
fields.深度上限: It only talks about "can the basis be explained clearly" and does not talk about explainability technical methods.
fields.安全与伦理边界: For judgments involving rights and interests, people have the right to know the basis and question the results.
fields.通俗解释:
Let the AI explain clearly "what information I based this judgment on" - if it can explain it clearly, it will be explainable; if it cannot explain it clearly, don't rush to believe it no matter how beautiful the reason is. Interpretability means that the operating mechanism and output basis of the AI ​​system can be understood and explained by others. The direction of specializing in this is called explainable AI (XAI).
It's a bit like a good doctor prescribing medicine: he doesn't just throw you a box of medicine and that's it, but he explains why he prescribes it and what the basis is. It is the same reason to ask AI tools to explain the basis for judgment.
There is one thing that is easy to misunderstand: being explainable does not necessarily mean it is accurate. An AI may be able to explain things succinctly, but the conclusion is still wrong; conversely, an AI with correct conclusions may not be able to explain things clearly. Interpretability and correctness are two different things, and neither can guarantee the other. When encountering a result that cannot be explained but requires you to believe it first, be more cautious.

fields.精确定义: Privacy refers to an individual’s right to control and be free from intrusion over the collection, observation, use and disclosure of his/her information; personal information protection refers to the legal requirements and safeguards established around the collection, processing, storage, transmission and deletion of personal information.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "it is absolutely safe as long as it is anonymous" (multi-source data combination may still re-identify individuals); "there are no restrictions as long as the user agrees".
fields.典型案例: When uploading homework photos, I found that there were classmates’ faces and names in the background.
fields.反例: Send the list including name, address, and photo directly to the public group.
fields.深度上限: It only makes judgments about "which information cannot be entered, cannot be disclosed, and whether consent is required" without going into the details of legal provisions.
fields.安全与伦理边界: No information such as students’ real identities, voices, portraits, locations, accounts, etc. may be collected, uploaded or disclosed without authorization (red line in Master §8.2).
fields.来源依据: China's Personal Information Protection Law and Data Security Law; NIST AI RMF Privacy Definition
fields.通俗解释:
Before sending a homework photo, take a look at the background: Are there any classmates’ faces or names written in it? At this glance, there is a sense of privacy. Privacy means that individuals have control over the collection, observation, use, and disclosure of their own information and are free from intrusion; personal information protection refers to the legal requirements and safeguards established around the collection, processing, storage, transmission, and deletion of information.
There’s a hidden pitfall: Don’t think that being anonymous means you’re absolutely safe. The principle of a jigsaw puzzle - one piece alone cannot tell what it is, but if data from different sources are put together, it is still possible to re-identify a person. "The user agrees" does not mean that everything can be done, and consent does not mean unlimited authorization.
In practice, just remember three things: what information cannot be input into AI, what information cannot be made public, and whether you need to ask for permission before using other people’s information. Don’t even think about sending a list of names, addresses, and photos to a public group.

fields.精确定义: Copyright is the exclusive right (reproduction, dissemination, adaptation, etc.) granted to creators by law; signature is the practice of identifying the creator and source of a work or content, and is a basic requirement for academic and creative integrity.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "AI-generated content must be copyright-free or must belong to the user"; "AI does not need to be noted".
fields.典型案例: When quoting Internet images, indicate the author and source, and confirm whether use is allowed.
fields.反例: Put pictures downloaded from the Internet into your work without citing the source.
fields.深度上限: We only make judgments about "whether it can be used, whether it should be marked, and how to mark it." We do not talk about legal exceptions and precedents.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Sources, authorizations, citations, attribution, and secondary use boundaries must be stated (Master §8.3).
fields.来源依据: Master §8.3 Materials and Copyright; China's "Measures for Labeling of Synthetic Content Generated by Artificial Intelligence"
fields.通俗解释:
If you see a good picture online and want to include it in your own work, you must first go through two procedures: confirm whether it is allowed to be used, and indicate who the author is and where it comes from. Behind these two procedures are two things: Copyright is the exclusive right granted by law to creators over their works, and reproduction, dissemination, and adaptation are all left to the creator; signature is the practice of indicating the source of the work and content, which is a basic requirement for academic and creative integrity.
Regarding AI-generated works, there are two extremes that are untenable: one says "AI-generated content must have no copyright" and the other says "the content must belong to the user" - the actual situation is not absolute, and it depends on the specific situation. Don’t think that “you don’t need to indicate the source anyway if you use AI.” You cannot skip the step of indicating the source.
When borrowing a book from a classmate, you need to ask and tell who it belongs to when using it. This is how you respect the work.

fields.精确定义: Deep fakes are audio, video, and image content generated or tampered with AI, which can make characters appear falsely in appearance or voice.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "only professional teams can make it" (the threshold for tools continues to decrease, and identification and prevention are more important).
fields.典型案例: Use the tool to swap someone's face onto another video.
fields.反例: Just because someone's face appears in the video, it is assumed that they did it.
fields.深度上限: It only makes judgments about "identifying risks, not producing, not distributing, and asking adults for help" without explaining the principles of detection technology.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Do not produce or disseminate content in which others have changed their faces or forged voices; if you find suspected forged content, you should stop disseminating it.
fields.来源依据: China's "Regulations on the In-depth Integration of Internet Information Services" (Effective in 2023); Master Version §8.3
fields.通俗解释:
The face in the video and the voice in the voice may not be who they are at all. Deep forgery refers to audio, video, and image content generated or tampered with AI, which can make a person appear falsely in appearance or voice. For example, using a tool to swap someone's face onto another video makes it look like they actually did that thing.
This is a bit like high imitation of fake paintings: no matter how similar the handwriting is, it is still a fake painting. Don’t think that only professional teams can afford it—the threshold for tools has been lowering, and ordinary people can get started, so identification and prevention are more important than before.
Remember this: just because someone’s face appears in the video, it doesn’t mean they did it. When encountering suspicious audio or video images, be suspicious first, don’t forward them, and ask the adults around you. You can't even make it yourself or spread it. This line is untouchable.

6-07.name: Safety Boundary and Human Decision Points

fields.精确定义: Identify systemic risks, conditions that must be stopped or rolled back, and steps that must be decided, verified, or approved by humans.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is that "if there is no problem with AI, there is no need to set boundaries"; "no error reporting" is regarded as "no risk".
fields.典型案例: If you find that your input contains other people's privacy, stop it immediately and delete it.
fields.反例: Ignore the inspection process in order to keep up with the schedule.
fields.深度上限: It only makes judgments about "identifying risks, stopping, protecting information, and seeking adult help" and does not simulate professional decisions.
fields.安全与伦理边界: High-risk matters such as health, legal, financial, personal safety and identity evaluation only learn to identify risks, stop actions, protect information and seek help from qualified adults.
fields.通俗解释:
When working on AI projects, don’t wait until something goes wrong before scrambling. Decide on three things in advance: which risks are considered systemic risks, under what circumstances must be stopped or rolled back, and which links must be decided, verified, and approved by humans. These three things taken together are the safety boundary and the artificial decision point.
There are two mistakes that are most likely to be made: one is to think that "AI has no problem, why set boundaries"; the other is to regard "no error reported" as "no risk". Error reporting is the machine reminding you. Many risks do not report errors and require human inspection to see them. You don't have to wait for a car crash to find the brakes, they have to be installed beforehand.
When it comes to trivial matters: if you find that someone else’s privacy is included in your input, you should stop and delete it immediately; even if you are rushing to make progress, you will not skip the check step.

fields.精确定义: Identify interests and impacts, respect boundaries, reserve human decisions and take responsibility for the results of use and publication.
fields.常见误解: The misunderstanding is "AI generated, problems are not mine"; "AI marked" is regarded as exemption.
fields.典型案例: Before the project is released, answer five questions: "Where does the data come from, who verifies it, who affects it, who makes the decision, and whether it should be released."
fields.反例: Put the responsibility on the tool.
fields.深度上限: We only make judgments about "who is responsible and on what basis" and do not talk about the legal responsibility system.
fields.安全与伦理边界: Responsibility cannot be transferred to AI; projects must not be represented as usable or releasable without passing the responsibility gate.
fields.来源依据: Master version §6.3 Third level responsibility access control; §2.4 Responsibility performance
fields.通俗解释:
If AI does the work for you, who will be responsible if something goes wrong? It's yours. Tools do not take the blame: the responsibility falls on the person who makes the decision and presses the publish button.
